docs.title: Interface
docs.text:
import stim
from autoqec_sim import noise as nm
from autoqec_sim.noise import presets

noisy = nm.apply(skeleton, presets.forte(), scale=0.25)           # ion, parallel
noisy = nm.apply(skeleton, presets.chain(timing="sequential"), 1.0)
noisy = nm.apply(skeleton, presets.board(), 1.0, n_data=n)         # board recipe
noisy = nm.apply(skeleton, presets.heron(graph=nm.heavy_hex(4, 4)), 1.0)

prof = presets.heron().with_bias(10.0)                            # eta = pZ/(pX+pY)
prof = prof.with_timing(nm.partial(4))                            # 4 two-qubit gates per slot
prof = prof.with_params(correlated=nm.Correlated(crosstalk=1e-4))
f = nm.noisifier(prof, scale=0.5)                                 # circuit -> noisy circuit
dem = nm.dem(noisy)                                               # board options; approximate only if stim requires

apply(circuit, profile, scale, *, n_data=None, idle_qubits=None, check_graph=True). Every probability of the profile is multiplied by scale; durations and coherence times are not. The input must be noiseless (nm.strip_noise first for a committed board circuit). With a graph on the profile, every two-qubit gate is checked against it and a ConnectivityError listing the violations is raised; check_connectivity returns the list without raising.

Profile(name, params, timing, graph) bundles:

Field Content Params.p2, bias2, pauli2 two-qubit gate error, its bias, or an explicit 15-vector in stim PAULI_CHANNEL_2 order Params.p1, bias1 single-qubit unitary error and bias Params.p_reset, p_meas X_ERROR after R and Z_ERROR after RX; flip probability on M and MX Params.idle Idle(kind="duration", T1, T2) or Idle(kind="slot", gate, meas) or kind="none"; scope "all" or "data"; optional bias for scalar slot rates Params.leakage Leakage(per_meas_layer, per_2q, mode="pauli"/"heralded", herald_detectors) Params.correlated Correlated(gate_pairs=((pauli2, rate), ...), exclusive, crosstalk, crosstalk_pauli) Params.t_2q, t_1q, t_meas, t_reset layer durations by instruction class, seconds Profile.timing PARALLEL, SEQUENTIAL, or partial(k) (Timing(gates_per_slot=k)) Profile.graph Graph from square, triangular, heavy_hex, complete (ion chain), path, or None for unconstrained

A rate set to None means no channel of that class (the board recipe has no single-qubit-gate channel); 0.0 emits the channel with probability 0, so scale sweeps keep the instruction structure (as ion_noise does).

docs.title: Placement per TICK segment
docs.text: After the timing rewrite (reslot: the non-two-qubit instructions of a layer stay together in a first slot, then the two-qubit gates k per slot; k=1 equals ion_noise.serialize_two_qubit), each segment emits its instructions unchanged, each followed by its channel: two-qubit gate, then DEPOLARIZE2(p2) or PAULI_CHANNEL_2, then the gate_pairs terms, then crosstalk terms, then per-gate leakage; single-qubit unitary, then DEPOLARIZE1(p1), PAULI_CHANNEL_1, or Z_ERROR (infinite bias); reset, then its flip; measurement with p_meas as the gate argument. If the segment did anything, one idle channel goes on every in-scope qubit not operated in it, and, if the segment measures, the per-measurement-layer leakage term on the same qubits. The idle duration is the slowest instruction class present in the layer.

docs.title: Channels
docs.text:
Single-qubit bias: px = py = p / (2 (1 + eta)), pz = p eta / (1 + eta); eta = 1/2 is depolarizing and is emitted as DEPOLARIZE1(p).

Two-qubit bias (product-weight construction): weights w(I) = w(X) = w(Y) = 1, w(Z) = 2 eta, probability of the pair P1 P2 proportional to w(P1) w(P2) over the 15 non-identity pairs, total p. Each single-qubit marginal has bias exactly eta; eta = 1/2 is the uniform depolarizing channel and is emitted as DEPOLARIZE2(p). At large eta the mass sits on ZZ (weight 4 eta^2), then equally on the six pairs with one Z factor (2 eta), then the eight Z-free pairs. This is a modelling choice with no measured decomposition behind it (no IonQ or IBM Pauli-twirled two-qubit decomposition is public); a measured 15-vector goes in Params.pauli2.

Correlated: gate_pairs are CORRELATED_ERROR lines after every two-qubit gate on its two targets, independent by default; exclusive=True chains them with ELSE_CORRELATED_ERROR using conditional probabilities q_i = p_i / (1 - sum_{j<i} p_j). Crosstalk: for every two-qubit gate (a, b) and every graph neighbour c of a or b outside the gate, one CORRELATED_ERROR(rate) with crosstalk_pauli[0] on the gate qubit and crosstalk_pauli[1] on c (default ZZ, a stochastic stand-in for always-on ZZ coupling or spectator drive). Spectators that are themselves in another gate of the layer are included.

Leakage: mode="pauli" is the erasure-to-Pauli proxy, DEPOLARIZE1(3/4 rate) (the qubit replaced by the maximally mixed state with probability rate, the simulation proxy of 1, Appendix E). mode="heralded" is HERALDED_ERASE(rate), stim's erasure with a flag bit in the measurement record, plus a DETECTOR per flag when herald_detectors (default), so the DEM carries the herald; the skeleton's rec[-k] references are rewritten around the extra records and nm.strip_noise removes the heralds again. Both are approximations: stim has no leaked state, and a leaked qubit is neither erased nor depolarized (its later gates apply non-Pauli errors on neighbours).

docs.title: DEM exactness
docs.text: The board's pinned derivation (derive_dem, approximate_disjoint_errors False) converts DEPOLARIZE1/2, X_ERROR, Z_ERROR, PAULI_CHANNEL_1 with three positive components, and independent CORRELATED_ERROR terms exactly. It refuses PAULI_CHANNEL_2 (any two-qubit bias other than 1/2, or pauli2), ELSE_CORRELATED_ERROR, HERALDED_ERASE, and a PAULI_CHANNEL_1 with a zero component. Profile.dem_exact says which case a profile is in; nm.dem(circuit) tries the exact conversion and falls back to approximate_disjoint_errors=True (error O(p^2) in the merged probabilities, mechanism set unchanged), or raises with approximate=False. Board conformance (noise_recipe_errors) accepts only the board profile's output.

Builder Graph Notes heavy_hex(rows, cols) honeycomb of rows x cols hexagons with a qubit on every edge; max degree 3 IBM Eagle and Heron style. rows + 1 lines of 4 cols + 1 qubits plus connectors; 12 qubits per hexagon. check_connectivity(circuit, graph, layout=None) returns one Violation (layer, gate, qubits, reason) per two-qubit gate whose mapped pair is not an edge or touches a node outside the graph; apply raises ConnectivityError with the list. The [[9,1,3]] one-round circuits have 24 violations on any heavy-hex graph with the identity layout (the circuit uses one ancilla per check with all-to-all placement); a layout mapping is the caller's job.

docs.title: Use in the circuit-level reward
docs.text:
circuit_noise.resolve_noise_model accepts a autoqec_sim.noise.Profile (presets.forte(), presets.chain(), presets.board(), presets.heron(), presets.depolarizing(p), or any with_bias, with_timing, with_params variant), a preset name, or a bare stim.Circuit -> stim.Circuit callable. The encoding gate list is laid out as a TICK-layered skeleton (as-soon-as-possible scheduling) so the profile's timing model and idle channel apply; every noise instruction the profile emits becomes a fault mechanism, propagated through the rest of the circuit (a GF(2) product against the symplectic map of the circuit suffix, which fault_set_reference reproduces with stim's PauliString.after) and scored with the Knill-Laflamme kernel as -(undetected mass), normalized by the total mass. A profile without a graph takes the environment's graph; a profile whose graph differs is refused, and a two-qubit gate off the graph raises ConnectivityError (or scores violation_reward with on_violation="penalize"). dem_undetected_mass cross-checks the result against stim's detector error model to O(p^2). Use through make_circuit_level_reward(env, profile) as a terminal reward (reward_mode="sparse"); it is per circuit, not batched.

docs.title: CPU profile of the vectorized simulator
docs.text:
Throughput and memory of the batched tableau, the Knill-Laflamme reward, and CodeDiscoveryEnv, measured by benchmarks/profile_tableau.py (stdlib and numpy; no torch). This is a numpy profile on the host CPU of one laptop, not the GPU-vectorized simulator the roadmap's week-4 wording names; the cuQuantum kernels have not been written (README, "What is left for cuQuantum").

Machine: macOS-26.5.1-arm64-arm-64bit, Apple M5 Pro, 18 logical CPUs, BLAS threads capped at 6 (OMP_NUM_THREADS, OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS, MKL_NUM_THREADS, VECLIB_MAXIMUM_THREADS); Python 3.12.14, numpy 2.5.3 (BLAS: accelerate). Whole run: 24 s on 2026-09-21.

Setting per cell: all-to-all graph, gates H, S, CNOT (actions is the size of the action table), k = 1, reward = normalized Knill-Laflamme term over every Pauli of weight 1 and 2 (errors) plus the weight-1 stabilizer penalty, the reward of the rediscovery regression. Rates are batch elements per second: one ActionTable.apply call on a batch of B is B gate applications, one reward call is B reward evaluations, one env.step is B env steps (the env_steps axis of the PPO agent). Each rate is the mean over at least 0.3 s of repeated calls after one warm-up call, on a machine that was otherwise idle. The tableau column is 2n (2n + 1) bytes of uint8 per element; the reward column is the peak of the (B, M, n + k) float32 product and its int64 copy inside undetected_mask, 12 M (n + k) bytes per element. Cells whose intermediate exceeds the cap are not run; the gate rate does not depend on the reward and is measured everywhere.

docs.title: Where the time goes
docs.text:
The reward and the gate kernels are timed inside env.step; the pieces of the Knill-Laflamme term are timed on their own on the same arrays, and their sum is within measurement noise of the term.

piece (n = 16, batch = 1024) ms per call share of env.step env.step 37.14 100% ActionTable.apply 0.24 1% reward 36.81 99% Knill-Laflamme term 35.19 95% weight-1 stabilizer penalty 1.61 4% code_rows and float32 casts 0.30 1% GEMM (M, 2n) x (2n, n + k) 5.41 15% int64 cast and & 1 (mod 2) 10.01 27% two any() reductions over n + k 19.36 52% und @ lam and normalization 0.36 1%

At n = 16, batch 1024, the reward is 99% of an environment step and the gate kernels 1%; the remainder is env.step bookkeeping (history, masks, reset of finished elements). Inside the Knill-Laflamme term the float32 GEMM of the error set against the code rows is 15%, the int64 cast for the mod-2 reduction 28%, and the two boolean any() reductions over the (B, M, n + k) product 55%, so the README's list is right that the symplectic product of the error set against the code rows is the hot path but not that the GEMM is the whole of its cost: on this CPU the mod-2 cast and the reductions on the product are most of it. A bit-packed popcount product with the parity and the commutation test fused into one kernel would remove the GEMM, the cast, the reductions, and the (B, M, n + k) intermediate, which is also the memory bottleneck (GiB per batch at n >= 25 against kilobytes for the tableau itself). The gate kernels run at 1 to 9 million gate applications per second and are under 3% of a step at every n (the ratio of the env-steps and gate-applications columns); they are not what a GPU port has to speed up first.

docs.title: Rediscovery regression
docs.text:
uv run autoqec-regress --budget reduced          # what the pytest runs
uv run autoqec-regress --budget full --out experiments/regression/regression.json

States evaluated up to a verified rediscovery at the full budget, seed 0, for the three targets both agents share, with each run's wall time next to its marker (experiments/regression/figure.py draws it from the two result files):

Targets (all k = 1, d = 3):

Target Graph Gates Max gates Forbidden stabilizer weights [[5,1,3]] 12 all-to-all on 5 H, S, CNOT 14 1 Steane [[7,1,3]] 3 all-to-all on 7 H, S, CNOT 20 1 to 3 rotated surface [[9,1,3]] 4 3x3 square lattice H, CNOT 30 1 rotated surface, LDPC w_max = 4, deg_max = 4, env mask 3x3 square lattice H, CNOT 30 1 rotated surface, LDPC w_max = 4, deg_max = 4, penalty 0.25 3x3 square lattice H, CNOT 30 1 Steane, LDPC w_max = 4, penalty 0.25 all-to-all on 7 H, S, CNOT 20 1 to 3 7 qubits, LDPC w_max = 3, penalty 0.25, must fail all-to-all on 7 H, S, CNOT 20 1 5 qubits, LDPC w_max = 3, penalty 0.25, must fail all-to-all on 5 H, S, CNOT 14 1

The two exclusion targets pass when no verified distance-3 code is found within budget. On 5 qubits this is a theorem: the [[5,1,3]] code is the unique 5-qubit distance-3 code and all 15 of its nontrivial stabilizers have weight 4, so w* = 4 and no w_max = 3 solution exists. On 7 qubits it is empirical: Steane and the second [[7,1,3]] family the search finds both have w* = 4, and no [[7,1,3]] code generated by weight-3 elements was found in the recorded budget; the contrast target steane_ldpc_w4 finds Steane in the same budget. w_max = 4 does not exclude the [[5,1,3]] code or Steane (both have w* = 4), which is why the bound for the exclusion targets is 3; on 9 qubits w_max = 4 does exclude Shor's code 5 (w* = 6). Exclusion targets forbid only weight-1 stabilizers so weight-2 and weight-3 generators stay admissible, and use the penalty form so that the search path is unconstrained and only the final code is judged. Every verification reports min_max_generator_weight (w*) and max_qubit_degree.

Reward during search: normalized Knill-Laflamme 6 reward over all Paulis of weight 1 and 2, plus the penalty on stabilizer elements of the forbidden weights (without it the agent pads a [[5,1,3]] code with idle qubits and still satisfies the [[7,1,3]] and [[9,1,3]] parameters). A success is verified independently of the reward: the circuit is replayed, the code is extracted, its distance is computed exactly, and its weight enumerators of S and N(S) are compared with the reference code. Equal enumerators are necessary for equivalence under qubit permutations and local Cliffords; they are reported as enumerators_match_reference, not as a proof of isomorphism. The full budget restarts with the next seed until the enumerators match; the reduced budget stops at the first verified nontrivial [[n,1,3]] code and reports whether it matched.

Results of the full run are in experiments/regression/regression.json (seeds, budgets, evaluations, wall time, the found circuits and stabilizers). Summary of the release run (seed 0, batch 512, at most 100,000 circuit evaluations per attempt, up to 60 attempts; exclusion targets run 5 seeds to exhaustion):

Target Gates Attempts (seeds) Circuit evaluations Wall time Found code w* / degree Enumerators match [[5,1,3]] H, S, CNOT 1 (seed 0) 13,824 1.1 s d = 3, 14 gates, non-CSS 4 / 4 yes Steane [[7,1,3]] H, S, CNOT 3 (seeds 0 to 2) 54,272 29.8 s d = 3, 19 gates, non-CSS as generated 4 / 4 yes rotated surface [[9,1,3]] H, CNOT 21 (seeds 0 to 20) 60,416 20.9 s d = 3, 22 gates, non-CSS as generated 6 / 4 yes rotated surface, LDPC mask w_max = 4 H, CNOT 10 (seeds 0 to 9) 78,848 44.3 s d = 3, 28 gates, non-CSS as generated 4 / 4 yes rotated surface, LDPC penalty w_max = 4 H, CNOT 1 (seed 0) 10,752 11.3 s d = 3, 30 gates, non-CSS 4 / 4 no (not required) Steane, LDPC penalty w_max = 4 H, S, CNOT 1 (seed 0) 67,584 47.4 s d = 3, 18 gates, non-CSS as generated 4 / 5 yes 7 qubits, LDPC penalty w_max = 3 H, S, CNOT 5 (seeds 0 to 4) 501,760 154.9 s none (expected); best reward -3/210 on every seed n/a n/a 5 qubits, LDPC penalty w_max = 3 H, S, CNOT 5 (seeds 0 to 4) 501,760 62.2 s none (expected); best reward -3/105 on every seed n/a n/a

The w* column is the exact minimum bottleneck generator weight of the found code: the unconstrained surface-code run returned a code with the surface enumerators but w* = 6, that is, a code whose sparsest generating set has a weight-6 element, so equal enumerators do not certify local-Clifford equivalence to the CSS reference (a local Clifford preserves weights, so an equivalent code would have w* = 4; the enumerators of S and N(S) coincide without equivalence here). That weight enumerators are not a complete invariant is well known: the classification of self-dual additive codes over GF(4) lists 675 inequivalent codes at 9 qubits with 320 distinct enumerators 7, and local-Clifford equivalence has a polynomial-time test 8. The regression reports the enumerator match as a necessary check, and w* as a second invariant. The mask-constrained run matched the enumerators with w* = 4 in 10 attempts against 21 unconstrained. The penalty-constrained surface target accepts any verified distance-3 code within the bound: in a first full run it produced one on all 60 attempts (31 distinct enumerator classes, none the surface code's; kept in the JSON under first_run_attempts), so the surface code is one of many weight-4 [[9,1,3]] codes reachable on the lattice and a stop-at-first search rarely lands on it. On the exclusion targets the best reward stayed at three undetected weight-2 errors on every seed, that is, the search kept codes within w_max = 3 that miss distance 3 by three errors rather than taking the 0.25 penalty of a weight-4 solution.

"Non-CSS as generated" means the found generators mix X and Z; the enumerators equal those of the CSS reference, consistent with a local Clifford equivalence, which the check does not prove. Attempts that ended in a verified nontrivial [[n,1,3]] code with different enumerators are kept in the JSON under attempts. The reduced budget (batch 256, 15,000 evaluations per attempt, at most 3 attempts, 1 seed for exclusion targets, no enumerator requirement) finishes all eight targets in about 60 s and is what tests/test_regress.py runs.

Hit rates from tallies of independent seeds (batch 512, 60,000 evaluations per run, every run produced a verified nontrivial [[n,1,3]] code): on 7 qubits all-to-all the search finds two families, with stabilizer enumerators [1,0,0,0,21,0,42,0] (Steane) and [1,0,0,0,13,24,18,8]; Steane appeared in 35 of 80 runs (H, S, CNOT and H, CNOT gate sets behave alike). On the 3x3 lattice the [[9,1,3]] codes are far more varied: the rotated-surface enumerators appeared in 3 of 60 runs with H, CNOT and in 0 of 30 runs with H, S, CNOT, which is why the surface target uses H, CNOT and the full budget allows up to 60 attempts.

docs.title: PPO agent
docs.text:
agents/ppo.py is a PPO implementation 9 over CodeDiscoveryEnv, in the spirit of 10: a policy over gate choices conditioned on the current tableau, trained on the Knill-Laflamme reward. The batch dimension of the environment is the vectorized environment (256 parallel episodes by default), auto_reset is on, and the reward is the dense mode (state reward after every gate). An episode ends when the state reward reaches 0 (every term of the reward is satisfied) or after the target's gate cap.

Network and hyperparameters (PPOConfig defaults):

Item Value Observation the 2n x 2n X and Z bits of the whole tableau (destabilizers and stabilizers, sign column dropped), mapped to {-1, +1}; check_matrix (only the (n - k) x 2n stabilizer block, as in 10) is an option Network MLP trunk, two tanh layers of 256 units, orthogonal init; linear policy head over the action table and linear value head sharing the trunk. 99,615 parameters for [[5,1,3]] (100 inputs, 30 actions), 130,873 for Steane (196 inputs, 56 actions), 157,730 for the 3x3 surface target (324 inputs, 33 actions). policy="auto" (the default) switches to the permutation-equivariant per-qubit network from 12 qubits on; see "Policy choice" below Rollout 16 steps of 256 environments, so 4,096 transitions per update Optimization Adam, learning rate 3e-4, 4 epochs, minibatch 512, gradient norm clipped at 0.5 PPO clip 0.2, gamma 0.98, GAE 11 lambda 0.95, value coefficient 0.5, entropy coefficient 0.01, advantages normalized per update Masking the action table already contains only the gates the graph allows, so no graph masking is needed there; graph_action_mask builds a static mask when a table has actions outside a graph; a dynamic mask forbids undoing the previous gate when it is an involution (H, CNOT, CZ, SWAP, Paulis); an action_mask() method on the environment, if present, is intersected with these. Masked actions get logit -1e9 Threads CPU only, torch and BLAS capped at 6 threads

Run on one target, or the regression:

uv run --extra rl python -m autoqec_sim.agents.ppo --n 5 --max-steps 14 --verbose
uv run --extra rl autoqec-ppo --budget reduced
uv run --extra rl autoqec-ppo --budget full --out experiments/regression/regression_ppo.json

(autoqec-ppo is the console script for autoqec_sim.agents.ppo_regress.)

Policy choice. PPOConfig.policy selects the actor-critic from agents/policies.py: "mlp" is the flat network of the table above; "equivariant" is a per-qubit permutation-equivariant network (a shared MLP over the qubit's two tableau columns plus a mean-pooled context, per-gate heads on the qubit embedding for single-qubit gates and on the ordered pair of embeddings for two-qubit gates, value head on the pooled embeddings, 128 units, 123,907 parameters on the 4x4 lattice against 344,897 for the flat MLP); "auto", the default, is equivariant when the environment has n >= 12 qubits and mlp otherwise, so the regression targets (n <= 9) keep the networks and results above. The equivariant policy is the recommendation for n >= 12: in the scaling probe it reaches a clean [[16, 1, 4]] in 217k to 258k env steps on 3 of 3 seeds where the flat MLP at batch 256 never does; the flat MLP at n >= 12 needs 1024 parallel episodes and ent_coef = 0.001 (4.2M to 4.7M steps). Both take the same observation and masks from EnvAdapter and emit logits in the order of the action table; PPOAgent.policy holds the resolved choice and the result's config["policy_resolved"] records it.

ppo_regress uses the same targets, reward (Knill-Laflamme plus the low-weight-stabilizer penalty), replay, and verification (exact distance, enumerators of S and N(S) against the reference) as regress. The difference in protocol: a PPO run does not stop at its first success; every distinct code the policy produces (deduplicated by the reduced row echelon form of its stabilizer block) is verified, and the full budget stops at the first code whose enumerators match, moving to the next seed only if a run exhausts 3,000,000 state evaluations or 20 minutes. The reduced budget (400,000 state evaluations, 90 s, one seed) stops at the first verified nontrivial [[n,1,3]] code and is what tests/test_ppo.py runs on the [[5,1,3]] target (1.5 s).

Results of the full run, seed 0, in experiments/regression/regression_ppo.json, against the evolutionary search's experiments/regression/regression.json on the same targets. Circuits are episodes for PPO and evaluated sequences for the evolutionary search; state evaluations are reward calls per batch element (one PPO environment step of the batch is 256 of them; one evolutionary circuit costs up to max gates of them, so its count is an upper bound).

Target Agent Seeds Circuits State evaluations Wall time First d = 3 code (circuits) Enumerators match [[5,1,3]] evolutionary 1 13,824 about 193,000 1.1 s 13,824 yes [[5,1,3]] PPO 1 4,352 61,440 1.4 s 4,352 yes Steane [[7,1,3]] evolutionary 3 54,272 about 1,085,000 28.9 s 22,528 yes Steane [[7,1,3]] PPO 1 11,264 225,280 10.7 s 3,841 yes rotated surface [[9,1,3]] evolutionary 21 60,416 about 1,812,000 20.5 s 1,024 yes rotated surface [[9,1,3]] PPO 1 3,333 106,496 3.4 s 1,025 yes

On the fair axis (state evaluations) PPO needs 3 times fewer for [[5,1,3]], 5 times fewer for Steane, and 17 times fewer for the surface code; per state evaluation it is slower (network forward and backward on top of the reward kernel), so the wall-time gap is smaller. The Steane run saw the same two 7-qubit families as the evolutionary tallies ([1,0,0,0,13,24,18,8] five times before Steane once). The surface run produced 11 distinct enumerator families among 13 verified codes before the rotated-surface enumerators appeared, at a per-episode success rate of 60 percent by update 26; with the evolutionary search that family appeared in about one run in twenty. The matched surface circuit has 15 gates against 22 for the evolutionary one. Seeds 1 to 3 at the full budget also matched every target on the first attempt: 53,000 to 66,000 state evaluations for [[5,1,3]], 119,000 to 160,000 for Steane, and 61,000 to 176,000 for the surface code (3 to 12 s per target). The evolutionary column is one run from one seed sequence, not an average.

The 4x4 target. ppo_regress.PPO_ONLY_TARGETS adds rotated_surface_16: [[16, 1, 4]] on the 4x4 lattice with H and CNOT, 50-gate episodes, weight-1 stabilizers forbidden, the regression's reward (normalized Knill-Laflamme term over the 16,248 Paulis of weight at most 3 plus the padding penalty) and match criterion (enumerators of S and N(S) against known_codes.ROTATED_SURFACE_16, w* = 4, degree 4). It runs in the full budget only, with its own budget of 1,000,000 env steps in one attempt (TARGET_BUDGETS; the reduced budget skips it), and policy="auto" resolves to the equivariant network (123,907 parameters). Two seeds at 2 threads (autoqec-ppo --budget full --targets rotated_surface_16 --seed S --threads 2, experiments/regression/regression_ppo_4x4_seed{0,1}.json; the machine was shared with other sessions at a load of 20 to 150, about 830 env steps per second):

Seed Env steps Episodes Wall time First verified [[16,1,4]] Distinct [[16,1,4]] codes verified Enumerators match Success rate, last 25 updates 0 1,003,520 19,968 1,203 s 88,576 env steps (93 s), 46 gates, non-CSS, w* = 5, degree 6 66 no 0.006 1 1,003,520 19,968 1,237 s 268,288 env steps (312 s), 48 gates, non-CSS, w* = 6, degree 5 2 no 0.000

Both seeds reach distance 4 within the range the scaling probe reported for this policy (217k to 258k env steps on the level distance reward), so the equivariant policy solves the 4x4 exploration problem under the regression's reward as well. Neither seed matches the rotated surface enumerators in 1M steps, so rediscovered is false for this target: the 68 verified codes fall into 68 distinct enumerator families, all non-CSS, and the trained policy does not consolidate on distance-4 states under this reward (0 to 3 percent of episodes per quarter of the run, against 56 to 64 percent after 1M steps on the level distance reward in experiments/scaling/REPORT.md). At 3x3 the surface enumerators appeared after 11 families; at 4x4 the family count is far larger and a stop-at-match search at this budget does not land on the CSS code. What the target does certify is a verified [[16, 1, 4]] code on the lattice in under 300k env steps on both seeds.

Missing for parity with 10:

  • Noise-aware training at larger scale. The noise-aware experiment below trains on the circuit-level fault reward under three profiles at n <= 16; a channel-weighted code-level error set (ErrorSet.from_channel) has not been used as a training reward.
  • Larger n and k > 1. The flat MLP input grows as 4 n^2 and the all-to-all action space as O(n^2); the equivariant policy removes the first but not the second, there is no attention policy and no curriculum over error weight, and the reward cost grows as 3^w C(n, w). k = 1 has been exercised at n <= 16 (the rediscovery regression at n <= 9, the scaling probe at n = 16); k > 1 only in the failed LDPC runs of the scaling probe.
  • Training conveniences: no learning-rate annealing, no checkpointing or policy export, no evaluation of a trained policy on a different graph (the static graph mask exists and is unit-tested but has not been used for transfer).
  • The undo mask is a heuristic of this implementation, not part of Olle et al.

docs.title: Related work
docs.text: What exists around each part of this package, as of October 2026, from a survey that walked the reference lists of the closest papers, the papers citing them, and the surrounding topics. Every entry below was checked against its arXiv or publisher record. Items with public code are marked.

docs.title: Automated code and encoder discovery
docs.text:
The gate-by-gate formulation this package's search layer uses, an agent appending Clifford gates to a stabilizer tableau under a Knill-Laflamme reward with the connectivity graph as the action space, is that of 1, whose code, QDX, is public and reached distance-5 codes at 11 to 17 qubits and a [[20,13,3]] code; composite "gadget" actions extend it to distance 7 23. The same simulator and agent were turned to fault-tolerant state preparation for a fixed code in 4 (code public). Earlier reinforcement learning for codes deformed a surface code toward a target logical error rate 5 and discovered few-qubit feedback strategies 6; later work searched tensor network code geometries 78 and reduced stabilizer weights toward LDPC codes 9. Variational discovery of codes and encoders predates the tableau formulation: a Knill-Laflamme loss on connectivity-constrained circuits 1011, neural-network code states 12, autoencoders 13, state-distinguishability losses with device runs 14 and their extensions to concatenation and logical operations 1516 (code public), Riemannian optimization over code subspaces 17, and variational graphical codes 18. Equivariant policies over tableaux appear in Clifford synthesis 19; the non-cumulative-objective RL of 20 is benchmarked on the same encoder task.

Evolutionary search for codes exists at the gate-sequence level 21 and over binary stabilizer strings to 20 qubits 22, and annealing reaches 50 qubits 23. Exact and exhaustive methods frame the problem differently: additive codes over GF(4) 24, the classification of self-dual additive codes 25, every stabilizer code to 9 qubits 26, all distance-3 codes 27, codeword-stabilized search as clique finding 28, and, in 2026, SAT: code design with hardware and physics constraints, proved NP-complete and solved to 100 qubits 29 (code public), phantom codes 30, and machine-checked distance certificates 31. Above 20 qubits the field designs codes by program evolution with large language models 323334 (the IBM code is public), by multi-agent orchestration with circuit-level evaluation 35, by Bayesian optimization with a learned logical-error predictor 36 (code public), by game-theoretic search 37, with decoders in the loop 3839, with hardware calls in the reward 40, and by multi-agent RL that includes a syndrome-extraction agent 41. Sparse codes can also be grown from seeds 42.

Where this package stands: its search layer is a reimplementation of 1 in numpy with a torch path, at parity on the distance-3 targets of QDX's published set and behind it on larger ones (experiments/qdx_targets/REPORT.md). Its evolutionary agent is simpler than 22. Nothing in its discovery mode is new.

docs.title: Noise- and hardware-tailored codes
docs.text:
Codes tailored to biased noise are a mature line: the XY and XZZX surface codes 4344, Clifford deformations, uniform and per-qubit 4546, bias-tailored LDPC codes 47, and in 2026 per-qubit deformation optimized from calibration data 48 (code public). Picking a small code from device error data goes back to 49 and was benchmarked against hardware in 50; distance choice from drifting calibration appears in 51, an ion-chain noise model with tailored extraction circuits in 52, and a full-stack empirical comparison in 53. The device presets here (Forte 54, a long ion chain 55, Heron 5657) and the heavy-hex lattice 58 are the inputs this package evaluates codes against.

Where this package stands: its reward is the undetected single-fault mass of the encoding circuit under such a profile, and its memory objective is a multi-round experiment with a decoder. The nearest prior objectives are code-capacity 14948 or circuit-level for a fixed code 4; 35 evaluates at circuit level inside a closed LLM loop. The comparison in experiments/sat_codes/REPORT.md shows the two levels ranking the same codes differently.

docs.title: Encoder synthesis and fault-tolerant preparation
docs.text: For a fixed code, SAT-optimal fault-tolerant state preparation 59, tableau-search encoders for arbitrary stabilizer codes 60, noise-aware LDPC encoder resynthesis 61, SMT search for fault-tolerant Clifford circuits 62, architecture-aware stabilizer synthesis 63, and heuristic and optimal CNOT and Clifford synthesis 64 (code public) all compete with RL-found encoders on gate count, and 64 claims to win. A benchmark for AI-assisted synthesis 65 and a FAIR circuit library 66 appeared in 2026.

docs.title: Syndrome-extraction schedules
docs.text: Hook errors and CNOT ordering are as old as the surface code 6768. Automated scheduling is a 2026 topic: Monte Carlo tree search with decoder feedback 69 (code public), MaxSAT-guided rewrites 70 (code public), SMT depth-optimal compilation 71, RL rewarded by sampled logical error rate 72, left-right circuits with effective-distance proxies 73, hook-free surface-code schedules 74, short Shor-style sequences 75, flag-style extraction for small codes 76, detector-error-model-driven design 77, and the result that hypergraph-product codes keep their distance under any schedule 78. The schedule synthesizer here is RL over the CX-layer assignment with the exact circuit-level fault distance as the reward, which none of these use; its one result, on the [[49,13,4]] entry of 79, is a demonstration rather than a benchmark against them.

docs.title: Distance, verification, and simulation
docs.text: Exact distance here is enumeration to 20 qubits. Public tools go further: randomized information-set distance 80, parallel Brouwer-Zimmermann 81, and SAT, MILP, and heuristic code and circuit distance in one package 82; the problem is NP-hard 83, has been cast as quantum annealing 84, and for large LDPC codes is bounded from above by heuristic witness search 85. Weight enumerators are not a complete invariant, and local-Clifford equivalence has its own test 2586; the generator weight this package calls w* is the optimal generator weight of 87. Fault-counting sensitivities 88, Pauli diagnostics 89, and tensor-network enumerators 90 are further evaluation tools. Stim 91 underlies the noise and detector-error-model work; Clifft 92 is the Unitary Foundation's near-Clifford sampler; 93 reports hardware error-detection experiments from the same group.

docs.title: Reproducing the rediscovery regressions
docs.text:
Two regressions rediscover the [[5,1,3]], Steane [[7,1,3]], and rotated surface [[9,1,3]] codes (plus the LDPC-constrained and exclusion targets for the evolutionary search): autoqec-regress (evolutionary search over gate sequences) and autoqec-ppo (PPO). Each has a reduced budget, run by the test suite and by tools/reproduce.sh, and a full budget, whose results ship in experiments/regression/regression.json and experiments/regression/regression_ppo.json and are tabulated in README.md. Every run records seed, budget, platform, numpy and torch versions, and thread count in its JSON.

Search is randomized but seeded: the same seed, batch size, numpy version, and thread count reproduce the same circuits and evaluation counts. Across numpy versions or BLAS libraries the random streams are identical (numpy default_rng), but PPO's torch arithmetic can differ in the last bits and change a trajectory; expect the PPO counts to move, not the outcome.

docs.title: Clean environment
docs.text:
uv venv --python 3.12 .venv-repro && source .venv-repro/bin/activate
uv pip install --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu "torch>=2.14.0"   # CPU torch
uv pip install "autoqec-sim[rl] @ git+https://github.com/unitaryfoundation/autoqec-sim@v0.2.0"  # or ".[rl]" in a checkout
export OMP_NUM_THREADS=6 OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=6 MKL_NUM_THREADS=6

docs.title: autoqec_sim.backends.torch_backend
docs.text:
torch versions of the tableau gate kernels and of the parity masks.

Every function here has the name and the semantics of its numpy counterpart in autoqec_sim.tableau, autoqec_sim.symplectic, and autoqec_sim.reward, but takes and returns torch.Tensor objects on whatever device the tableau lives on (cpu or cuda). The tableau layout is the same (batch, 2n, 2n + 1) uint8 array, so torch.from_numpy(tab) and tab.cpu().numpy() move a state between the two backends without conversion.

Parity test. The numpy path computes the float32 product of the error set against the code rows, casts it to int64, masks the low bit, and runs two boolean any() reductions; on the CPU the cast and the reductions are about 80 percent of the reward (docs/profile.md). Here the product is reduced mod 2 in place in float32 (remainder_(2), exact because the entries are integers below 2n) and the two commutation tests are one matrix-vector product against a weight vector: stabilizer columns weigh 2k + 1 and logical columns 1, so the score of an error is s (2k + 1) + l with s the number of anticommuting stabilizers and l the number of anticommuting logicals, and the error is undetected iff 1 <= score <= 2k (s = 0 and l >= 1). The intermediate is one float32 (batch, chunk, n + k) block, a third of the numpy path's peak, and no boolean (batch, chunk, n + k) array exists at all.

Gate kernels are the gather and scatter operations of the numpy module on torch tensors. Grouping a vector of actions by gate type needs one nonzero per gate type, which on cuda synchronizes with the host; the gate kernels are about one percent of an environment step, so this is accepted rather than fused.

docs.title: autoqec_sim.agents.ppo
docs.text:
Proximal policy optimization over the batched code-discovery environment.

The agent follows Olle et al. (arXiv:2311.04750) in spirit: a policy over discrete gate choices, conditioned on the current stabilizer tableau, and trained on the Knill-Laflamme reward that the environment returns at every step. The batch dimension of autoqec_sim.env.CodeDiscoveryEnv is the vectorized environment; one call to env.step advances every episode by one gate.

Components (Schulman et al., arXiv:1707.06347):

  • clipped surrogate objective with ratio clip clip_eps;
  • generalized advantage estimation with gamma and gae_lambda;
  • a value head sharing the trunk with the policy, squared-error loss weighted by vf_coef;
  • an entropy bonus weighted by ent_coef.

Action masking. The environment's action table already contains only the gates the connectivity graph allows, so nothing there needs masking. The agent still applies a mask through EnvAdapter: (i) a static mask from graph_action_mask when the table has actions on edges outside a given graph (a policy trained on all-to-all and evaluated on a lattice), (ii) a dynamic mask that forbids undoing the previous gate when it is an involution (H, CNOT, CZ, SWAP, Paulis), and (iii) any mask the environment itself exposes through an action_mask() method returning a (batch, num_actions) boolean array. Masked actions receive the logit MASK_LOGIT (a large negative number) before sampling.

Policies. PPOConfig.policy chooses the actor-critic from autoqec_sim.agents.policies: the flat MLP ("mlp"), the per-qubit permutation-equivariant network ("equivariant"), or "auto" (the default: equivariant from 12 qubits on, mlp below). Both take the same observation and mask from EnvAdapter and return logits in the order of the environment's action table plus a value.

torch is imported lazily so that the rest of the package works without it.

docs.text:
Actor-critic networks for the PPO agent.

Two policies share the interface model(obs, mask=None) -> (logits, value) with obs the flat {-1, +1} observation of autoqec_sim.agents.ppo.EnvAdapter, mask an optional boolean (batch, num_actions) tensor, logits of shape (batch, num_actions) in the order of the environment's action table, and value of shape (batch,). Relabelling the qubits permutes the logits accordingly. This is the policy the RL scaling probe found to reach [[16, 1, 4]] on every seed where the flat MLP at batch 256 never did (experiments/scaling/REPORT.md).

resolve_policy implements the "auto" choice of autoqec_sim.agents.ppo.PPOConfig: the equivariant network from EQUIVARIANT_MIN_QUBITS qubits on, the flat MLP below.

docs.text:
Search agents over gate sequences, evaluated in batches by the environment.

EvolutionarySearch keeps a population of fixed-length action sequences (-1 entries are no-ops, so sequences may be shorter than the cap). Every generation is one batched rollout. The next population is the elite, mutated children of tournament-selected parents (point replacement, insertion, deletion, one-point crossover), and a fraction of fresh random sequences. With random_frac = 1 it degenerates to random search.

A PPO agent over the same environment is in autoqec_sim.agents.ppo (optional torch dependency).

docs.title: autoqec_sim.regress
docs.text:
Known-code rediscovery regression.

For each target the search agent, from a seeded start, must produce an encoding circuit on the target's connectivity graph whose code has the target parameters [[n, 1, 3]] with no stabilizer element below a target-specific weight (so a smaller code padded with idle qubits does not count). The result is verified independently of the reward: the circuit is replayed, the code is read off the tableau, its distance is computed exactly, and its weight enumerators are compared with the reference code. Equal enumerators of S and N(S) are a necessary condition for equivalence under qubit permutations and local Cliffords; the report labels the match as such rather than as a proof of isomorphism.

LDPC targets add the sparsity constraint of autoqec_sim.ldpc (Target.ldpc): a hard bound w_max on the generator weight enforced in the environment (mode "mask" or "terminate") or as a reward penalty (mode "penalty"). Two of them are exclusion targets (expect_success=False): the search must not find a distance-3 code within budget. For 5 qubits with w_max = 3 this is a theorem (the [[5,1,3]] code is unique and every nontrivial stabilizer has weight 4); for 7 qubits with w_max = 3 it is an empirical statement bounded by the budget, contrasted with w_max = 4, which admits the Steane code and is found in the same budget. The verification of every LDPC target reports min_max_generator_weight (exact w*) and the maximum qubit degree of the sparsest basis found.

Run autoqec-regress --budget full for the release numbers (restarts until the enumerators match) and --budget reduced for the quick check that the pytest uses.

docs.title: autoqec_sim.tableau
docs.text:
Batched Aaronson-Gottesman stabilizer tableaux.

The state of the whole simulator is one dense array of shape (batch, 2n, 2n + 1) with dtype uint8. Row r < n is destabilizer r and row n + r is stabilizer r. Columns [0, n) hold the X bits, columns [n, 2n) the Z bits, and column 2n the sign bit (1 means the Pauli carries a minus sign). A qubit with X bit 1 and Z bit 1 is Y.

The tableau of the identity circuit has destabilizers X_0, ..., X_{n-1} and stabilizers Z_0, ..., Z_{n-1}. Applying a Clifford circuit C turns stabilizer row r into C Z_r C^dagger and destabilizer row r into C X_r C^dagger. In the encoding convention of Olle et al. (arXiv:2311.04750) the first k qubits carry the logical state and the remaining n - k start in |0>, so after the circuit the stabilizer rows k, ..., n - 1 generate the code and rows 0, ..., k - 1 of the stabilizer and destabilizer blocks are the logical Z and X operators.

Every gate routine takes an index array of batch elements and, per selected element, the qubit(s) to act on. The routines use only gather and scatter operations along the batch axis and elementwise XOR and AND, so each one maps to a single array kernel; there is no Python loop over the batch.

GF(2) linear algebra and the symplectic representation of Pauli operators.

A Pauli operator on n qubits (up to phase) is a binary vector of length 2n: the first n entries are the X bits, the last n the Z bits. Two Paulis commute iff their symplectic product x . z' + z . x' is zero mod 2. Batched products are computed with float32 matrix products followed by a parity reduction, which maps to a GEMM kernel; the entries never exceed 2n so float32 is exact.

docs.text:

Full (2n, 2n + 1) tableau in the encoding convention from a set of n - k independent commuting stabilizer generators.

Rows 0 .. k-1: logical X (destabilizer block), rows k .. n-1: destabilizers of the code stabilizers, rows n .. n+k-1: logical Z, rows n+k .. 2n-1: the given stabilizers (with signs).

The destabilizers solve the linear system <D_i, S_j> = delta_ij and <D_i, L> = 0 for every logical L (consistent because the rows S, L are independent), then are made mutually commuting by adding S_i to D_j whenever <D_i, D_j> = 1 for i < j; adding S_i changes no other product already fixed.

docs.title: autoqec_sim.env
docs.text:
Batched code-discovery environment with gymnasium-style semantics.

The state is one batched tableau of shape (batch, 2n, 2n + 1); every batch element is an independent episode. Actions are Clifford gates: the single-qubit gates on every qubit and the two-qubit gates on both orientations of every edge of a connectivity graph. The reward is any callable f(tab, k) -> (batch,), by default the Knill-Laflamme reward of autoqec_sim.reward. There is no dependency on gymnasium; reset and step follow its calling convention (observation, reward, terminated, truncated, info).

An optional LDPC constraint (ldpc_w_max) restricts the search to states whose stabilizer group has a generating set with every generator of weight at most w_max (autoqec_sim.ldpc.ldpc_feasible, exact for n - k <= 14). Mode "terminate" ends the episode of an element that leaves the feasible set with ldpc_violation_reward; mode "mask" reverts such an action to a no-op (the step is still counted) and CodeDiscoveryEnv.feasible_action_mask gives agents the full per-action mask; mode "final" leaves the path free and only withholds success from an infeasible state (the constraint binds the solution, not the trajectory). A soft alternative is the reward term autoqec_sim.ldpc.make_ldpc_penalty. terminated is true when an episode ends by success or by violation; info["success"] distinguishes them.

docs.title: autoqec_sim.reward
docs.text:
Knill-Laflamme rewards, vectorized over a batch of tableaux.

Following Olle et al. (arXiv:2311.04750, Eq. 10), an error E_mu is detected by the code with stabilizer group S if it anticommutes with some stabilizer generator or lies in S (a degenerate error acts trivially). K_mu = 0 in that case and 1 otherwise, and the reward is r = -sum_mu lam_mu K_mu. Detecting every Pauli of weight < d is equivalent to the Knill-Laflamme conditions for correcting all errors of weight at most (d - 1) // 2, since the conditions involve products E_a^dagger E_b of two such errors.

Membership in S is decided without linear algebra: a Pauli that commutes with all n - k stabilizer generators lies in the normalizer, and it lies in S iff it also commutes with all 2k logical operators, because the logicals form a symplectic basis of N(S) / S. So K_mu = 1 iff E_mu commutes with every stabilizer row and anticommutes with at least one logical row. Both tests are one batched symplectic product of the error set against the n + k relevant rows of the tableau.

docs.title: autoqec_sim.ldpc
docs.text:
LDPC sparsity of a stabilizer group, batched over tableaux.

Two quantities of a stabilizer group S with m = n - k generators:

w* (minimum bottleneck weight) The smallest w such that the elements of S of weight at most w generate S; equivalently the smallest possible maximum generator weight over all generating sets. For m <= exact_max_generators (default 14) it is computed exactly: all 2^m group elements are enumerated as bit-packed uint64 rows, sorted by weight, and a batched GF(2) elimination gives the rank of the elements of weight <= w. The pivot rows of that elimination, restricted to weight <= w*, are a generating set with maximum weight w* (the sparsest basis reported here; it is a minimum-bottleneck basis, not necessarily a minimum-total-weight one). For larger m the fallback is a greedy pairwise reduction of the given generators (replace g_i by g_i g_j whenever that lowers its weight, to convergence); its maximum weight is an upper bound on w*.

deg (maximum qubit degree) The largest number of generators of the sparsest basis acting on one qubit. The degree depends on the basis; the value reported is that of the basis above, so it is an upper bound on the minimum achievable maximum degree at bottleneck weight w*.

The exact path costs O(2^m) memory per batch element and 2n vectorized elimination steps; at n = 9 and batch 512 one call takes a few milliseconds, cheap enough to run every environment step. Bit packing needs 2n <= 64.

LdpcObjective combines the Knill-Laflamme term, the padding penalty, and the sparsity constraint into the reward and the success criterion of an LDPC-constrained [[n, k, d]] target, in one of the forms of LDPC_FORMS (compared at n = 12 and 16 in experiments/ldpc_scaling/REPORT.md; DEFAULT_LDPC_FORM is the one that comparison selected; the shaped and terminal forms and greedy_action_mask are the sparsity variants of experiments/ldpc_sparsity/REPORT.md; its "exact" method, the feasibility test after every two-qubit action on the pairs the greedy bound rejects, is the exact-mask section of that report).

docs.title: ExactMaskCache
docs.text: Bounded cache of the light group elements of a stabilizer group for greedy_action_mask with method="exact", keyed by the bytes of the packed greedy basis (the same tableau gives the same basis, so a state seen again, such as the initial state after a reset, is not enumerated twice). Oldest entries are evicted above maxsize.

docs.title: LdpcObjective
docs.text:
Reward f(tab, k) -> (batch,) and success criterion success(tab, k, state_reward) -> (batch,) bool of an LDPC-constrained [[n, k, d]] target with bottleneck bound w_max (and optionally a qubit-degree bound deg_max).

Base terms on every state: the Knill-Laflamme term over the Paulis of weight below d (autoqec_sim.reward.kl_reward) and the padding penalty (autoqec_sim.reward.low_weight_stabilizer_penalty at weight 1). A candidate is a state with every error detected and no idle qubit. Forms:

"penalty" The rediscovery regression's form: normalized base (fraction of undetected errors, fraction of weight-1 Paulis in S) plus -scale * excess on every state. Success iff the reward is 0. At n >= 12 one undetected error is worth 1/630 to 1/1128 against scale = 0.25 per unit of w* excess, and PPO converges to sparse groups of distance 1 (experiments/scaling/REPORT.md). "unnormalized" Per-error base: the number of undetected errors and the number of weight-1 stabilizers, one unit each, plus -scale * excess, so that one undetected error costs 1 / scale units of w* excess. The sum is divided by r0, the number of undetected errors of the initial state (|0> ancillas, bare logical qubits), a global constant that keeps the reward within about [-1, 0] for the value head and changes neither the optimum nor the normalized-advantage policy gradient. Success iff the reward is 0. "final" Normalized base only; the constraint is hard and terminal: success iff the state is a candidate with exact w* <= w_max. No sparsity signal on the trajectory. "schedule" Distance first. Normalized base until activate is called (the trainer does so once the success rate at the target distance exceeds a threshold); from then on the penalty form. Before activation success is any candidate, after it the reward must be 0. "shaped" The unnormalized base divided by r0 minus shaping * excess in reward units on every state (greedy bound on ordinary states, exact on candidates), so that one unit of w* excess costs shaping * r0 undetected errors (3.75 to 15 at [[12, 2]] for shaping 0.05 to 0.2, against 0.25 in the unnormalized form). Success iff the reward is 0. "terminal" Count-unit terminal signal. Ordinary states get the unnormalized base divided by r0 and no sparsity term; a candidate ends the episode with reward 1 - h / m, where h is the number of generators of the sparsest basis with weight above w_max (heavy_generator_count, exact) and m = n - k, so one excess generator costs one unit out of m and a feasible code scores 1. Success (episode end) is any candidate; feasibility is h = 0, which feasible and the experiment check.

Cost. On ordinary states w* is the greedy pairwise-reduction bound of this module (a few ms per batch; equal to the exact value on 95 to 99 percent of random states); on candidate states the exact w* replaces it (2^(n - k) group elements, exact_generators at most), where it decides success. last holds the terms of the last evaluated batch for diagnostics.

docs.title: greedy_action_mask
docs.text:
greedy_action_mask(
    tab: ndarray,
    k: int,
    action_table,
    w_max: int,
    method: str = "basis",
    exact_max_generators: int = EXACT_MAX_GENERATORS,
    cache: ExactMaskCache | None = None,
    stats: dict | None = None,
    chunk_rows: int = 1 << 22,
) -> np.ndarray

(B, num_actions) bool: false where the action would take the stabilizer group outside the bound w* <= w_max. Single-qubit gates never change the support of a stabilizer, so they are always allowed. Three methods; the first two are upper bounds on w* (the mask can forbid an action whose exact w* is within the bound; it never allows one outside), the third is exact:

"tableau" every two-qubit action is applied to a copy of the whole tableau batch and _greedy_stats runs from the tableau's generators on all copies in one call (0.13 s for 132 CNOT actions at n = 12, batch 256; 7 s for 600 at n = 25, most of it the copies and the packing). The method of the runs of experiments/ldpc_sparsity/REPORT.md at n = 12. "basis" the current state's greedy basis is computed once ((B, m) packed rows), every CNOT is applied to those packed rows with two bit operations (_packed_cnot), and _greedy_within re-reduces only the rows the gate made heavy (a CNOT raises the weight of a Pauli by at most one). No tableau copies; the cost scales with the number of heavy rows. Requires the two-qubit actions to be CNOTs (falls back to "tableau" otherwise). "exact" the "basis" bound as a pre-filter, then the exact feasibility test on every (state, action) pair the bound rejected: the group after the gate has a generating set within w_max iff the elements the gate leaves at weight <= w_max have rank m = n - k, decided by _exact_cnot_admits over the elements of weight <= w_max + 1 of the current group (the only ones a CNOT can bring within the bound), enumerated once per state and shared by all its actions (cache keeps them across calls for states seen again); the rank test is over the heavy rows of the gate-transformed basis only, since the light rows are in the light span already. Needs m <= exact_max_generators; above that the method is "basis" (stats["method"] records which ran). Two-qubit gates other than CNOT are tested exactly on tableau copies of the rejected pairs (ldpc_feasible).

stats, when given, receives the counts of the call: two-qubit pairs, pairs the greedy bound rejected, pairs tested exactly (and how many of them were distinct, since identical states in the batch share one test per action), pairs the exact test admitted, cache hits and misses, and the seconds spent in the greedy and the exact parts.

docs.title: autoqec_sim.circuit_noise
docs.text:
Circuit-level noise for the reward, wired to autoqec_sim.noise.

A noise model is any callable stim.Circuit -> stim.Circuit that inserts Pauli noise into a noiseless encoding circuit. Three forms are accepted wherever a noise model is expected (see resolve_noise_model):

  • a autoqec_sim.noise.Profile (presets.board(), presets.chain(), presets.forte(), presets.heron(), presets.depolarizing(p), or a variant built with with_bias, with_timing, with_params), applied through autoqec_sim.noise.noisifier(profile, scale);
  • a preset name ("board-rfc0001", "chain-2606.06455", "forte-2308.05071", "heron-r2");
  • a plain callable, such as the placeholder depolarizing_noise_model, which is kept for tests and as the profile-free fallback.

The encoding circuit handed to the noise model is the gate list laid out in the TICK-layer convention of the noise module (gates_to_layered_circuit, as-soon-as-possible scheduling: a gate joins the earliest layer after the last gate on any of its qubits). The profile's timing model then decides how a layer maps onto time slots (parallel, sequential, or k two-qubit gates per slot), and its idle channel is charged to every qubit not operated in a slot. The profile's connectivity graph, when present, is the environment's graph (Graph.to_topology); a two-qubit gate on a non-edge makes the noise module raise ConnectivityError.

The reward enumerates every fault mechanism of the noisy circuit (each Pauli term of each noise instruction with its probability, the same mechanism set that stim's detector-error-model derivation walks, before merging by detector signature), propagates the mechanism through the remaining gates (a GF(2) product against the symplectic map of the circuit suffix; fault_set_reference does the same with stim's PauliString.after and is kept as the cross-check), and scores the resulting Pauli on the encoded state with the batched Knill-Laflamme kernel. Heralded mechanisms (HERALDED_ERASE) count as detected. The reward is -sum_f p_f K_f over mechanisms, divided by sum_f p_f when normalized. A detector-error-model derivation of the same undetected mass is provided for cross-checks (dem_undetected_mass); it is not used in the reward because an encoding circuit has no detectors of its own and the logical X and Z readouts needed to see both kinds of logical fault anticommute, so they need two circuits.

docs.title: FaultSet dataclass

docs.text:
fault_set(noisy_circuit: Circuit, n: int) -> FaultSet

Propagate every single fault of noisy_circuit to the end.

Handles DEPOLARIZE1/2, X/Y/Z_ERROR, PAULI_CHANNEL_1/2, CORRELATED_ERROR and ELSE_CORRELATED_ERROR chains (absolute probabilities), and HERALDED_ERASE (heralded). Annotations and TICK are ignored.

The propagation is symplectic: walking the circuit backwards keeps the 2n x 2n GF(2) map from a Pauli inserted at the current position to the output Pauli (signs dropped, they do not affect detection), each Clifford gate being a few row operations on that map, and the mechanisms of a noise instruction are one small GF(2) product against it. fault_set_reference is the instruction-by-instruction stim version it replaces; the two agree mechanism for mechanism.

docs.title: autoqec_sim.memory_objective
docs.text:
Multi-round memory objective: score a stabilizer code by the logical error rate of a syndrome-extraction memory experiment, not by its encoder.

The encoder single-fault objective of autoqec_sim.circuit_noise cannot see a local-Clifford deformation of a code (a Hadamard at the end of the encoder only relabels weight-1 faults, all detected), so it cannot express bias tailoring (experiments/noise_aware/runs/REPORT.md, verdict items 2 to 4 and 6). This module builds, for a code given by its stabilizer generators and logicals, an R-round syndrome-extraction circuit with one ancilla per generator, applies a autoqec_sim.noise.Profile with its timing model, derives stim's detector error model, and estimates the logical error rate per round with one of three fidelity tiers:

proxy closed form from the DEM: the failure probability of the maximum-likelihood decoder restricted to fault sets of weight at most two (pfail_low_weight, O(M^2) in the number M of DEM mechanisms, exact to O(p^3)), plus the exact circuit-level distance d_circ up to weight 4 and the mass of its minimum-weight undetectable logical fault sets (exact_dcirc, ported from ion-search/lib.py). No sampling, no decoder dependency. sampled small-shot Monte Carlo from the DEM with an exact maximum-likelihood decoder when detectors + observables <= exact_ml_bits (dynamic program over the joint syndrome distribution, 2^(D+O) table; the decoder's failure probability is then exact and no shots are needed), otherwise a lookup decoder built from the same weight-<= 2 fault sets with a one-mechanism completion for unseen syndromes. bposd full sampling with the board's pinned BP+OSD decoder (ldpc, optional dependency, validation only).

Circuits (build_memory_circuit). Every generator g_j gets an ancilla prepared in |+>, controlled-P gates (CX, CY, CZ) onto its support in a fixed order, then H and a Z-basis measurement. Generators that share a qubit with different Pauli letters cannot be interleaved (their controlled gates on that qubit do not commute), so the generators are colored into batches of mutually interleavable generators (for a CSS code: the X block and the Z block) which run one after another; inside a batch the gates are packed into layers as soon as possible with one gate per qubit per layer. Under the sequential timing of the ion presets every two-qubit gate is its own time slot anyway, so the batch structure costs nothing there. Preparation and final readout are noiseless MPP measurements of every generator and of the logical operators of the chosen basis (Z or X memory); detectors compare consecutive measurements of each generator, and the observables compare the initial and final logical readout. With flags="one" each generator of weight at least three gets a flag qubit (|0>, two CX from the ancilla around the middle of the support, measured and declared a detector) in the Chao-Reichardt pattern; flags need all-to-all connectivity here.

Connectivity (Layout). all_to_all_layout (the ion chain) places ancilla j on qubit n + j. square_layout(rows, cols) puts the data qubits on the lattice and ancilla sites at every plaquette center including the boundary ring, with edges only between a site and its corner data qubits (the rotated-surface-code hardware layout); generators are assigned to sites by a greedy minimum of the path lengths to their support, and a controlled gate to a non-adjacent qubit is routed along a shortest path with the nearest-neighbour CNOT ladder of the noise-aware experiment (intermediate qubits restored), so non-local generators pay in gates and depth. A generator that needs routing runs in a batch of its own. The profile's connectivity graph is replaced by the layout's graph, so the noise module's placement check applies to the routed circuit.

Reward (MemoryReward). The environment reward of the noise-aware experiment with the memory term in place of the encoder term: min(d, d*)/d* - 1 - q_1 on every state and, on states at the target distance with no weight-1 stabilizer, weight * log10(p_ref / p_round) clipped to +-clip decades, where p_round is the per-round logical error estimate of the chosen tier summed over the memory bases. Such a state ends the episode (the reward exposes success_fn, which autoqec_sim.env.CodeDiscoveryEnv picks up). Results are cached by the reduced row echelon form of the stabilizer block, so a code is evaluated once per run. The memory term depends only on the code, not on the encoding circuit that produced it.

docs.title: pfail_low_weight
docs.text:
pfail_low_weight(
    sig: Signature,
    max_weight: int = 2,
    max_triples: int = 2000000,
    exclusive: bool = False,
) -> float

Leading-order failure probability of the maximum-likelihood decoder restricted to fault sets of weight at most max_weight (2, or 3 when the number of triples is at most max_triples). Sets are grouped by syndrome, the decoder picks the observable pattern of largest summed weight per syndrome, and the rest fails. A set is weighted by prod_{i in set} p_i (the low-p asymptote, which does not damp a noisier circuit by the probability that nothing else happened); with exclusive the weight is the exact probability of that set alone, prod p_i prod_{j not in set} (1 - p_j). The leading term of the failure rate of a code whose circuit-level distance is at most 2 max_weight; meaningful while the expected number of faults per shot (sig.probs.sum()) is below about one.

Returns (p_fail, table) with table of shape (2^O, 2^D). The decision for syndrome s is argmax_o table[o, s]; p_fail = 1 - sum_s max_o table[o, s].

docs.title: Correlated dataclass
docs.text:
Correlated Pauli terms beyond the per-gate channel.

gate_pairs: ((pauli2, rate), ...) applied after every two-qubit gate on its (first, second) target as CORRELATED_ERROR; with exclusive the terms after the first become ELSE_CORRELATED_ERROR with conditional probabilities so exactly one of them can fire (the DEM conversion of the ELSE form needs approximate_disjoint_errors). crosstalk: for every two-qubit gate (a, b) and every graph neighbour c of a or b outside the gate, CORRELATED_ERROR(crosstalk) with crosstalk_pauli[0] on the gate qubit and crosstalk_pauli[1] on c. Stochastic stand-in for always-on ZZ coupling or spectator drive; needs Profile.graph.

docs.title: Idle dataclass
docs.text:
Idle channel of a layer, applied to every qubit in scope not operated in an active layer.

kind "duration": PAULI_CHANNEL_1(t / (4 T1), t / (4 T1), t / (2 T2)) with t the layer's wall-clock duration (slowest instruction class present). Pure dephasing from T2 plus a Pauli-twirled amplitude term, linear in t (t << T1, T2). The T2 here is the measured T2 (Hahn or Ramsey as the source states), used as a total dephasing time: the pz formula does not subtract the T1 contribution, which is the same convention as ion_noise. kind "slot": a fixed channel per layer class, gate for layers without a measurement and meas for layers with one. Each is a scalar (emitted as DEPOLARIZE1(rate), the board's form) or a 3-tuple (PAULI_CHANNEL_1(px, py, pz)). kind "none": no idle channel. scope "all": every qubit the circuit uses; "data": qubits 0..n_data-1 (the board rule; apply then needs n_data). bias: for scalar slot rates only, eta of the emitted channel (None or 1/2: DEPOLARIZE1(rate); otherwise PAULI_CHANNEL_1 with pz/(px+py) = eta; inf: Z_ERROR(rate)). Duration idles carry their own T1/T2 structure and tuple slot idles are taken as given.

docs.title: Leakage dataclass
docs.text:
Leakage, in a stim-expressible form.

Rates: per_meas_layer fires on every qubit not measured in a layer that measures (the mid-circuit-measurement leakage of arXiv:2606.06455 Table V); per_2q fires on both qubits of every two-qubit gate, after the gate's Pauli channel.

mode "pauli": the erasure-to-Pauli proxy, DEPOLARIZE1(3/4 rate), i.e. the qubit is replaced by the maximally mixed state with probability rate and nothing is heralded. This is the simulation proxy of arXiv:2606.06455 Appendix E. mode "heralded": HERALDED_ERASE(rate), stim's erasure channel with a flag bit in the measurement record; with herald_detectors a DETECTOR on each flag so the DEM carries the herald. This models detected leakage (leakage detection units or post-selection); the board's conformance check does not accept heralded channels, and the DEM conversion needs approximate_disjoint_errors.

Both are approximations: a leaked qubit is neither erased nor depolarized, it acts as a lost qubit whose gates with neighbours apply non-Pauli errors. Stim has no leaked state.

docs.title: Params dataclass
docs.text:
Rates at scale 1 (probabilities) and durations (seconds).

p2, p1: total Pauli error per two-qubit gate and per single-qubit unitary, with biases bias2, bias1 (eta = pZ / (pX + pY); 1/2 is depolarizing and is emitted as DEPOLARIZE1/2, any other value as PAULI_CHANNEL_1/2). pauli2, if given, is an explicit 15-vector in stim's PAULI_CHANNEL_2 order that overrides p2 and bias2. p_reset: X_ERROR after R, Z_ERROR after RX. p_meas: flip on M and MX. t_2q, t_1q, t_meas, t_reset: layer durations by instruction class.

Construction: rows + 1 horizontal lines of 4 cols + 1 qubits; vertical connector qubits join line i to line i + 1 at horizontal position x with x = 0 mod 4 on even i and x = 2 mod 4 on odd i. Every hexagon then has 6 degree-3 vertices and 6 degree-2 edge qubits (12 qubits). Line qubits are numbered first, row by row, then connectors. docs.title: autoqec_sim.noise.profile
docs.text:
Profile = parameter set + timing + connectivity graph.

Every probability in a Params is a rate at scale 1; apply multiplies all of them by scale. Durations and coherence times do not scale. A field set to None means "no channel of that class" (the board recipe has no single-qubit-gate channel); 0.0 means a channel that is emitted with probability 0 (so scale sweeps stay structurally identical, as in ion_noise).

docs.title: Idle dataclass
docs.text:
Idle channel of a layer, applied to every qubit in scope not operated in an active layer.

kind "duration": PAULI_CHANNEL_1(t / (4 T1), t / (4 T1), t / (2 T2)) with t the layer's wall-clock duration (slowest instruction class present). Pure dephasing from T2 plus a Pauli-twirled amplitude term, linear in t (t << T1, T2). The T2 here is the measured T2 (Hahn or Ramsey as the source states), used as a total dephasing time: the pz formula does not subtract the T1 contribution, which is the same convention as ion_noise. kind "slot": a fixed channel per layer class, gate for layers without a measurement and meas for layers with one. Each is a scalar (emitted as DEPOLARIZE1(rate), the board's form) or a 3-tuple (PAULI_CHANNEL_1(px, py, pz)). kind "none": no idle channel. scope "all": every qubit the circuit uses; "data": qubits 0..n_data-1 (the board rule; apply then needs n_data). bias: for scalar slot rates only, eta of the emitted channel (None or 1/2: DEPOLARIZE1(rate); otherwise PAULI_CHANNEL_1 with pz/(px+py) = eta; inf: Z_ERROR(rate)). Duration idles carry their own T1/T2 structure and tuple slot idles are taken as given.

docs.title: Leakage dataclass
docs.text:
Leakage, in a stim-expressible form.

Rates: per_meas_layer fires on every qubit not measured in a layer that measures (the mid-circuit-measurement leakage of arXiv:2606.06455 Table V); per_2q fires on both qubits of every two-qubit gate, after the gate's Pauli channel.

mode "pauli": the erasure-to-Pauli proxy, DEPOLARIZE1(3/4 rate), i.e. the qubit is replaced by the maximally mixed state with probability rate and nothing is heralded. This is the simulation proxy of arXiv:2606.06455 Appendix E. mode "heralded": HERALDED_ERASE(rate), stim's erasure channel with a flag bit in the measurement record; with herald_detectors a DETECTOR on each flag so the DEM carries the herald. This models detected leakage (leakage detection units or post-selection); the board's conformance check does not accept heralded channels, and the DEM conversion needs approximate_disjoint_errors.

Both are approximations: a leaked qubit is neither erased nor depolarized, it acts as a lost qubit whose gates with neighbours apply non-Pauli errors. Stim has no leaked state.

docs.title: Correlated dataclass
docs.text:
Correlated Pauli terms beyond the per-gate channel.

gate_pairs: ((pauli2, rate), ...) applied after every two-qubit gate on its (first, second) target as CORRELATED_ERROR; with exclusive the terms after the first become ELSE_CORRELATED_ERROR with conditional probabilities so exactly one of them can fire (the DEM conversion of the ELSE form needs approximate_disjoint_errors). crosstalk: for every two-qubit gate (a, b) and every graph neighbour c of a or b outside the gate, CORRELATED_ERROR(crosstalk) with crosstalk_pauli[0] on the gate qubit and crosstalk_pauli[1] on c. Stochastic stand-in for always-on ZZ coupling or spectator drive; needs Profile.graph.

docs.title: Params dataclass
docs.text:
Rates at scale 1 (probabilities) and durations (seconds).

p2, p1: total Pauli error per two-qubit gate and per single-qubit unitary, with biases bias2, bias1 (eta = pZ / (pX + pY); 1/2 is depolarizing and is emitted as DEPOLARIZE1/2, any other value as PAULI_CHANNEL_1/2). pauli2, if given, is an explicit 15-vector in stim's PAULI_CHANNEL_2 order that overrides p2 and bias2. p_reset: X_ERROR after R, Z_ERROR after RX. p_meas: flip on M and MX. t_2q, t_1q, t_meas, t_reset: layer durations by instruction class.

docs.text:
apply(circuit, profile, scale): the noisy circuit of a skeleton.

Placement per TICK segment of the (re-slotted) skeleton, in this order:

  • each instruction unchanged, followed immediately by its channel: two-qubit gate: DEPOLARIZE2(p2) or PAULI_CHANNEL_2(15 biased args), then the correlated gate-pair terms, then crosstalk terms on graph neighbours, then per-gate leakage; single-qubit unitary: DEPOLARIZE1(p1) / PAULI_CHANNEL_1 / Z_ERROR; R / RX: X_ERROR(p_reset) / Z_ERROR(p_reset); M / MX: flip probability p_meas as the gate argument;
  • if the segment did anything: one idle channel on every in-scope qubit not operated in the segment; then, if the segment measures, the per-measurement-layer leakage term on the same qubits.

With the ion presets this reproduces ion_noise.apply_ion_noise byte for byte (tests/test_ion_equivalence.py) and with the board preset circuit_tools.apply_noise (tests/test_board_equivalence.py).

Timing models: how a TICK layer of the skeleton maps onto time slots.

docs.title: autoqec_sim.noise.channels
docs.text:
Pauli channels parametrized by a total rate and a bias.

The bias of a single-qubit Pauli channel is eta = pZ / (pX + pY). The depolarizing channel has eta = 1/2. For two-qubit channels the package uses a product-weight construction: a weight w(I) = w(X) = w(Y) = 1, w(Z) = 2 eta per factor and probability proportional to w(P1) w(P2) for every non-identity pair. Its single-qubit marginals have bias exactly eta and eta = 1/2 gives the uniform two-qubit depolarizing channel. As eta grows the channel concentrates on ZZ (weight 4 eta^2), then equally on the six terms with one Z factor (ZI, IZ, ZX, ZY, XZ, YZ, weight 2 eta), then the eight Z-free terms (weight 1). This is a modelling choice, not a measured decomposition: it does not distinguish ZI from ZX, and it is not the product of two independent single-qubit biased channels (which would have no correlation). Callers with a measured 15-vector pass it through Params.pauli2.

docs.title: autoqec_sim.schedule_env
docs.text:
Syndrome-extraction schedule synthesis for a fixed CSS code, as an episodic MDP whose reward is the circuit's fault distance.

The code is fixed. What the agent chooses is the CX layer structure of one extraction round: which (check, data qubit) couplings happen in which time slot. That is the quantity the board's circuit tier scores (qldpc-challenge/verify/circuit_tools.build_css_memory: "The schedule -- the thing the tier scores -- is the CX layer structure"), and the one that moved the measured logical error rate by 5 to 300x in the project's matched pairs under a fixed code, noise model, and decoder.

Episode. The Tanner edges of H_X and H_Z are visited in a fixed order; at each step the agent picks a time slot for the current edge. A slot is feasible when no edge already in it shares the check or the data qubit (the layer must be a matching), and, without interleave, X edges use the first slots_x slots and Z edges the following slots_z so the two blocks never overlap in time and every detector is deterministic. With interleave the two blocks share one set of slots; a schedule whose detectors are not deterministic (the ordering criterion of the board's interleaved builder fails) is invalid and scored invalid_reward.

Reward. At the end of the episode the schedule is built into the board's memory experiment (research/circuit_autogen.build_memory), the canonical noise recipe is applied, stim derives the detector error model, and the fault distance is read either exactly up to weight exact_wmax (autoqec_sim.memory_objective.exact_dcirc, the right tier when the code distance is at most 4 or 5) or by the board's own randomized information-set search (circuit_tools.ris_dem, an upper bound). The reward is min_basis d_circ / d minus depth_penalty per CX layer beyond the lower bound, so a schedule that reaches the code distance in the fewest layers scores 1. d_circ is clamped to d: nothing above the code distance is credited, since the tier does not credit it either.

Everything the reward depends on is the board's code, imported from a checkout of qldpc-challenge (QLDPC_CHALLENGE environment variable, default ../qldpc-challenge beside this repository), so a schedule found here is scored exactly as the board would score it on submission.

The longer rediscover, verify, and score walkthrough is docs/examples/rediscover_and_score.py. README after clifft's: logo, badges, one-line install, short quick start; CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md (Contributor Covenant 2.1).

  • backends.cuda_kernels: two opt-in fused CUDA kernels (CuPy, NVRTC) behind the torch backend, a per-element gate kernel and a bit-packed popcount parity kernel; agreement tests against the torch path; benchmark script and A100 numbers in docs/gpu.md. First tagged release. Three additions on top of 0.1.0: the noise module in the circuit-level reward, an LDPC sparsity constraint, and a PPO agent with its own rediscovery regression.

  • The noise module ships as the autoqec_sim.noise subpackage: biased, correlated, and leakage-aware Pauli channels, device timing, topologies, and sourced presets for IonQ Forte, a long ion chain, IBM Heron, and the qldpc-challenge recipe. circuit_noise accepts a autoqec_sim.noise.Profile, a preset name, or any stim.Circuit -> stim.Circuit callable (resolve_noise_model); profiles run through autoqec_sim.noise.noisifier with scale. Gate lists are laid out as TICK-layered skeletons (gates_to_layered_circuit, as-soon-as-possible scheduling), so the profile's timing model and idle channel apply. Fault mechanisms are enumerated from every noise instruction the module emits (DEPOLARIZE1/2, X/Y/Z_ERROR, PAULI_CHANNEL_1/2, CORRELATED_ERROR and ELSE_CORRELATED_ERROR chains with absolute probabilities, HERALDED_ERASE as heralded, hence detected) and propagated through the remaining gates as before. dem_undetected_mass derives the same undetected mass from stim's detector error model of the circuit plus an ideal stabilizer and logical readout, used as a cross-check (agreement to O(p^2), the merging error of the DEM). The placeholder depolarizing_noise_model stays and gained an idle rate; with p1=None, p2=p, idle=p it reproduces the board preset mechanism for mechanism.

A profile without a graph takes the environment's graph in resolve_noise_model and make_circuit_level_reward; a profile whose graph differs is refused. heavy_hex(rows, cols) is now the autoqec_sim.noise honeycomb construction (rows x cols hexagons), not the earlier brick-wall one.
  • ldpc: bit-packed batched GF(2) elimination; exact minimum bottleneck weight w* (smallest w such that the weight-<= w elements generate the group) for n - k <= 14 by enumerating the 2^(n-k) group elements, a greedy pairwise generator reduction as the fallback bound; the sparsest basis and its maximum qubit degree; ldpc_feasible, ldpc_penalty, make_ldpc_penalty.
