  • tests/test_ppo.py (6 tests, skipped without torch; 15 items with the policy tests below), including a reduced-budget [[5,1,3]] rediscovery that trains PPO in about 1.5 s.
  • autoqec-ppo console script for the PPO regression (uv run --extra rl autoqec-ppo).
  • Noise-aware discovery experiment (experiments.noise_aware, run as python -m): PPO under three autoqec_sim.noise profiles (board depolarizing, Forte ion chain with sequential timing, Heron rates on the setting's graph) scaled to equal total fault mass, in three settings (7 qubits all-to-all with H, S, CNOT; 3x3 and 4x4 square lattices with H, CNOT), five seeds per cell. Reward: shifted distance reward (fractional below the target on 4x4) and the padding penalty of the regression, plus, on states at the target distance with no idle qubit, the circuit-level undetected fault mass (normalize=False, weight 2 / M_0) and the LDPC penalty at w_max = 4; such a state ends the episode through the new success_fn hook of CodeDiscoveryEnv. Per seed: the best and the most visited target-distance codes with exact d, pure-X and pure-Z distances, local-Clifford CSS-frame search, w*, enumerators, and the undetected mass under all three profiles (cross-evaluation); known codes (Steane, rotated surface, XZZX, Hadamard-deformed surface, Shor, transposed Shor at n = 9 and n = 16) with standard-form encoders routed onto the lattice and polished per profile; training-curve CSVs and figures (experiments.figstyle, one style); experiments/noise_aware/runs/REPORT.md.
  • RL scaling probe (experiments.scaling, run as python -m; report in experiments/scaling/REPORT.md, runs in experiments/scaling/runs/). Diagnosis of the 4x4 failure of the noise-aware experiment ([[16, 1, 4]], H and CNOT on the lattice, 50-gate episodes): a distance-4 state is reachable at 50 gates (evolutionary search finds one after 369k circuits) but rare (0 of 8192 random 50-gate sequences, 2 at d = 3), the default agent never evaluates one in 21M to 24M env steps, and its terminal states are no better than random on the padding term (8 idle qubits, 87 to 91 percent CNOT actions), so the failure is exploration, not credit assignment or representational capacity. Variants, one change each: a target-distance curriculum learns d = 3 at n = 16 but not d = 4; CZ plus plaquette macros reach d = 4 in 23k to 38k steps by raising the gate budget to about 200 per episode; a per-qubit permutation-equivariant policy (scaling.equivariant_actor_critic, 124k parameters) reaches a clean d = 4 at the 50-gate cap in 217k to 258k env steps on 3 of 3 seeds (71 to 110 s) and produces d = 4 codes in 56 to 64 percent of episodes after 1M steps; 1024 parallel episodes with entropy coefficient 0.001 reach it with the flat MLP in 4.2M to 4.7M steps; the baseline alone needs an 80-gate cap (3.1M and 5.4M steps) and fails at 60 and 70 in 30 minutes. The LDPC penalty form of the regression does not scale past n = 9: in 18 runs at n = 12 and 16, k = 2 and 4, on all-to-all and square graphs (penalty scales 0.25 and 0.05, flat and equivariant policies, 20 minutes each) no run reached a distance-3 code with w* <= 4; every policy converges to sparse stabilizer groups of distance 1, because the normalized Knill-Laflamme term pays 1/630 to 1/1128 per detected error against 0.25 per unit of w* excess.
  • Three-topology run matrix (experiments.topologies, run as python -m; report in experiments/topologies/runs/REPORT.md). The PPO agent alone, not the LLM meta-agent of milestone M2, on square, triangular, and heavy-hex lattices at two tiers (3x3 and 4x4; heavy-hex 1x1 with 12 qubits and 2x1 with 18, the nearest sizes the honeycomb construction allows), one objective ([[n, 1, 3]], no idle qubit, H and CNOT on lattice edges, 50-gate cap, level distance reward), PPOConfig defaults with policy="auto", three seeds per cell, 2M or 4M env steps and 12 min per run. Common metrics per cell: steps and wall time to first success, exact d, w*, qubit degree, CSS test, weight enumerators, undetected fault mass of the encoder under the Heron preset on the cell's graph and under the board preset, and the routed rotated surface encoder's mass where one exists. All 18 runs reached distance 3: within the first three updates on the 9-qubit lattices, 49k to 113k env steps at 12 and 16 qubits, 307k to 345k on the 18-qubit heavy-hex graph. tests/test_topologies.py (3 tests, skipped without torch).
  • circuit_noise.fault_set propagates fault mechanisms with a GF(2) product against the symplectic map of the circuit suffix (15 to 25 times faster than the stim PauliString.after loop, now fault_set_reference, which the tests compare against mechanism for mechanism); gates_to_layered_circuit builds the skeleton from text in one parse.
  • env.CodeDiscoveryEnv(success_fn=...): an optional success criterion replacing the reward threshold.
  • matplotlib in the dev dependency group (figures of the experiment).
  • Tests: 44 to 71 for these modules (noise wiring, DEM cross-check, ion timing ranking, heavy-hex rejection, graph round trip, LDPC statistics, constraint modes, regression); 78 with the PPO agent's 6 and the version check.
  • agents.policies: the two actor-critics of the PPO agent, the flat MLP (moved out of agents.ppo unchanged) and the permutation-equivariant per-qubit network of the scaling probe (moved from experiments.scaling.equivariant_actor_critic, now also accepting the check_matrix observation). PPOConfig.policy with values mlp, equivariant, and auto (the default: equivariant from 12 qubits on, mlp below, EQUIVARIANT_MIN_QUBITS), PPOConfig.equivariant_hidden (128), PPOAgent.policy and PPOAgent.build_model(), and policy_resolved in the result's config. Below 12 qubits the agent builds the same network from the same torch RNG state as before, so the reduced PPO regression reproduces docs/reproduce.md step for step (counts, gates, and per-update history checked). experiments.scaling keeps its recorded-run protocol (build the MLP, then swap the equivariant network in) so experiments/scaling/runs/ stays reproducible; it now passes policy="mlp" explicitly. Seven test functions (nine items) in tests/test_ppo.py, which now collects 15 items.
  • known_codes.rotated_surface(d) (the rotated surface code of any distance on the d x d grid, the builder the noise-aware experiment used) and ROTATED_SURFACE_16 ([[16, 1, 4]], w* = 4, degree 4) in the known-code table.
  • PPO-only rediscovery target rotated_surface_16 in agents.ppo_regress (PPO_ONLY_TARGETS): [[16, 1, 4]] on square:4x4 with H and CNOT, 50-gate episodes, the regression's reward and enumerator match, a budget of 1,000,000 env steps in one attempt (TARGET_BUDGETS), skipped by the reduced budget (REDUCED_SKIP); target_budget() and --threads. Result at 2 threads (experiments/regression/regression_ppo_4x4_seed{0,1}.json): both seeds reach a verified [[16, 1, 4]] code (88,576 and 268,288 env steps, 46 and 48 gates, non-CSS, w* 5 and 6), 66 and 2 distinct codes over 1M steps, none with the rotated surface enumerators, so the target is not rediscovered at this budget.
  • regress.verify computes w* exactly up to n - k = 15 (VERIFY_EXACT_GENERATORS), so the 4x4 target's codes report the exact bottleneck weight instead of the greedy bound.
  • ldpc.LdpcObjective: reward and success criterion of an LDPC-constrained [[n, k, d]] target in four forms (LDPC_FORMS): penalty (the regression's normalized form), unnormalized (one undetected error costs one unit against scale per unit of w* excess, divided by the initial state's undetected count), final (hard final-state constraint, no LDPC term in the reward), and schedule (distance first, penalty switched on by activate()). The exact w* is evaluated on candidate states only (every error detected, no idle qubit), the greedy bound elsewhere. DEFAULT_LDPC_FORM is the form the comparison below selected.
  • ldpc.LdpcObjective forms shaped (dense per-step term -shaping * excess in reward units, greedy bound on ordinary states, exact on candidates) and terminal (no path term; any candidate ends the episode with reward 1 - h / (n - k), h the number of generators of the sparsest basis above w_max); ldpc.heavy_generator_count (m minus the rank of the light elements, basis independent) and ldpc.greedy_action_mask (per-action greedy w* bound, all two-qubit trials in one batched call, single-qubit gates always allowed).
  • Sparsity comparison (experiments.ldpc_sparsity, run as python -m; report in experiments/ldpc_sparsity/REPORT.md, runs in experiments/ldpc_sparsity/runs/): shaped at c = 0.05, 0.1, 0.2, terminal, and mask against unnormalized at 1.5M env steps on [[12, 2, 3]] (all-to-all, square:3x4) and [[16, 4, 3]] (square:4x4), equivariant policy, on the RunPod pod's CPU with every run under the compute ledger's wrap. Measured: the fraction of terminal states at distance 3 with exact w* <= 4. On the two 12-qubit cells ([[16, 4, 3]] pending): the mask variant makes the bound a property of the policy on all_to_all:12 (three seeds: 91, 68, and 89 percent of the terminal states of the last 25 updates at distance 3, every one at w* = 4, 769 to 2,248 distinct feasible codes per run; the reference: 50 to 62 percent at distance 3, w* 5 to 6, none inside) and traps on square:3x4 (every terminal state at w* = 4 and distance 1); the same mask on top of the terminal reward (mask_terminal, seed 0) does it on both cells (95 and 98 percent at distance 3, all at w* = 4, 2,151 and 166 distinct feasible codes). shaped traps at distance 1 at every c; terminal alone collapses onto one dense code (h = 2, w* = 7 all-to-all; h = 3, w* 5 to 6 on the lattice) because it optimizes the heavy-generator count, not w*; unnormalized at 3M env steps keeps w* 5 to 6. DEFAULT_LDPC_FORM stays unnormalized (the mask is an environment constraint, not a form). The mask costs 1.3 to 2 times the wall time per env step.
  • experiments.ldpc_sparsity scaling preparation: --device cuda puts the policy, the PPO update, the reward's base terms (LdpcObjective(device= ...), the error set on the device as float32, tableau copied once per call) and the terminal-state distance on the torch device; four all-to-all cells (n16_k4_all_to_all, n20_k4_all_to_all, n25_k1_d4_all_to_all, n25_k1_d5_all_to_all) with per-cell d and episode length (CELL_SPECS), the greedy w* bound as the success test above 15 generators (w_star_test in the JSON), and a capped code description above 20 qubits. ldpc.greedy_action_mask(method="basis"), now the default, applies every CNOT to the current state's greedy basis as packed bit operations and re-reduces only the rows the gate made heavy (_packed_cnot, _greedy_within): 0.05 s against 4.1 s per step at n = 25, batch 256, same bound, sound against the exact test; the n = 12 runs used method="tableau", which stays available. First scaling runs (mask_terminal, seed 0, batch 1024, 3M env steps, A40 shared with another job): [[16, 4, 3]] and [[20, 4, 3]] on the all-to-all graph never reach a distance-3 terminal state (57 to 59 percent of two-qubit actions masked at the end, 823 and 520 env steps/s); the [[25, 1]] cells are queued behind the pod's other GPU work.
  • ldpc.greedy_action_mask(method="exact"): the exact feasibility test in the action mask for n - k <= 15. The greedy basis bound stays as the pre-filter; every (state, action) pair it rejects gets the exact test: a CNOT changes the weight of a Pauli by at most one, so the elements of weight <= w_max + 1 of the current group (enumerated once per state from the 2^(n - k) group elements, shared by all of the state's actions, kept across steps in an ExactMaskCache keyed by the greedy basis) are the only ones the gate can leave within the bound; the gate is admitted iff those it leaves at weight <= w_max span the heavy rows of the gate-transformed basis (a GF(2) rank over the coefficient bits, uint16 rows, weights from a 16-entry table on the local Paulis of the control and the target). Identical states in the batch share one test per action. Above 15 generators the method is the greedy basis bound and says so in stats; two-qubit gates other than CNOT are tested on tableau copies of the rejected pairs. Tests: equal to ldpc_feasible on every trial action, admits everything the greedy bound admits, admits some moves the bound forbids, cache hits on repeated states. experiments.ldpc_sparsity: --mask-method exact, the run JSON's mask entry with the pre-filter and final masked fractions, exact tests and admissions per call, and cache counts; bench-mask (cost per env step of the mask methods on one cell); run_name tags the exact method (_exact) and a batch other than 256 (_b1024); label carries the mask method and batch. Cost on the pod's CPU (6 threads, 96-core host at load 30 to 90 from other tenants): 0.6 s per env step on all_to_all:16 at batch 256 (0.2 s greedy pre-filter, 0.4 s exact test over 34,000 rejected pairs per call), 27 percent of the wall time; 0.08 s on square:4x4, 9 percent. Runs (mask_terminal, 3M env steps, exact mask at batch 256 on three seeds and at batch 1024 on one, greedy controls at batch 256; report section "Exact feasibility mask"): negative on both [[16, 4, 3]] cells. On all_to_all:16 the exact test admits 4 to 7 percent of the pairs the greedy bound rejects (masked 53 to 58 percent of two-qubit actions against 58 for the greedy control), so the bound was nearly exact and the constrained set itself blocks distance 3 under a 40-gate episode; one feasible [[16, 4, 3]] in 9M env steps over three seeds, half the terminal states at distance 2 at the end on seed 0 (greedy control: 6 percent). On square:4x4 it admits 12 to 30 percent (masked 31 to 39 against 42), and every run ends at distance 1. The greedy control at batch 256 is as negative as the earlier batch-1024 run, so the update count was not the confound. At batch 1024 the exact mask is negative on both graphs too (1.7 s per env step on the all-to-all cell, 29 percent of the wall time). n = 20 (n - k = 16) is beyond the exact range and, on this evidence, would not change with it; the routes left are a gate set that moves weight inside the feasible set (CZ, SWAP), a longer episode, or a curriculum from the distance-2 groups. The batch-1024 records of the scaling section were renamed to the _b1024 tag; the tableau-method square:4x4 record carries _tableau.
  • LDPC-form comparison (experiments.ldpc_scaling, run as python -m; report in experiments/ldpc_scaling/REPORT.md, runs in experiments/ldpc_scaling/runs/): the forms unnormalized, final, and schedule on [[12, 2, 3]] and [[16, 4, 3]] with w_max = 4, all-to-all and square graphs, three seeds each, equivariant policy, 1.5M env steps or 20 minutes per run (36 runs plus 4 scale variants). unnormalized learns distance-3 codes at n = 12 to 16 where the penalty form never did (61 to 69 percent of terminal states at distance 3 on five of six [[12, 2, 3]] runs) and is the only form that produced codes within the bound (3 of 12 runs, all [[12, 2, 3]], at 303k, 354k, and 950k env steps), as single episodes: its policies' codes stay at w* 5 to 6 (n = 12) and 7 to 8 (n = 16). final reaches distance 3 and never a sparse code (0 of 12); schedule switches its penalty on at 0.63M to 0.91M env steps at n = 12 and then falls into the penalty form's distance-1 trap (0 of 12). unnormalized is DEFAULT_LDPC_FORM; regress.LdpcSpec(mode="objective", form=...) puts any form on a regression target (make_reward returns the objective, env_kwargs(target, reward) its success_fn; both regressions pass it). Also existence constructions for both targets (experiments/ldpc_scaling/runs/existence.json: [[5,1,3]] plus Steane, and two copies of a searched [[8,2,3]] with w* = 4).
  • Tests: the 4x4 target and reference (tests/test_ppo.py), the four objective forms on known codes and in environment rollouts (tests/test_ldpc.py), one tiny run per form and the report tables (tests/test_ldpc_scaling.py).
  • benchmarks/profile_tableau.py and docs/profile.md: CPU throughput and memory profile of the vectorized simulator (numpy on the host, not the GPU version the roadmap names) for n in 5 to 49 and batch 256 to 4096: gate applications, reward evaluations, and environment steps per second, bytes per batch element of the tableau and of the reward's intermediate product, and a time breakdown of one environment step. The reward's (batch, M, n + k) float32 product and its int64 copy for the mod-2 reduction are the memory bottleneck (GiB per batch at n >= 25, against kilobytes for the tableau) and the GEMM plus that cast are where the time goes.
  • backends.torch_backend: the two hot paths of the reward engine on torch tensors on any device (cpu or cuda), opt-in, with the numpy path and its results unchanged. Gate kernels apply_h, apply_s, apply_s_dag, apply_x/y/z, apply_cnot, apply_cz, apply_swap, apply_gate, and an ActionTable with its lookup arrays on the device; symplectic_product, code_rows, undetected_mask, in_stabilizer_mask, batched_distance, kl_reward, distance_reward, low_weight_stabilizer_penalty, CompositeReward, and the make_* closures with the same names and semantics as the numpy ones; numpy_reward_adapter plugs a torch reward into CodeDiscoveryEnv. The parity test reduces the float32 product mod 2 in place and decides both commutation tests with one matrix-vector product against a weight vector, so the int64 copy and the two boolean any() reductions of the numpy path (about 80 percent of its reward time on the CPU) and the boolean (batch, M, n + k) array are gone; the peak intermediate is 4 M (n + k) bytes per element instead of 12 M (n + k). On CPU torch the reward runs 1.9 times faster than numpy at n = 9 and 2.3 times at n = 16 (batch 1024); the gate kernels, one to two percent of a step, run at about half the numpy rate. tests/test_torch_backend.py (43 items, skipped without torch) checks every kernel and every mask against numpy bit for bit on random tableaux and the known codes at n in 5, 9, 16.
  • benchmarks/profile_tableau.py: --backend {numpy,torch}, --device {cpu,cuda}, --json (record a run), --render (tables from records), --no-breakdown. docs/gpu.md: running the profile on a RunPod GPU, the A40 result (experiments/profile_pod/runs/), and what stays cuQuantum-specific.
  • Packaging for release: SPDX license metadata, ruff configuration, CI and release workflows, tools/reproduce.sh, docs/reproduce.md, CITATION.cff. The autoqec-ppo console script runs the PPO regression.
  • All-to-all ion-chain cells (experiments.ion_chain, run as python -m; report in experiments/ion_chain/runs/REPORT.md): the noise-aware 4x4 protocol of experiments.gpu_scale (equivariant PPO, batch 1024, 8M env steps, 40 min cap, three profiles calibrated to equal total fault mass, three seeds) with the graph changed to all_to_all:16, in two settings defined in the module (a2a16 with H, S, CNOT and a2a16_hc with H, CNOT, the lattice gate set). Imports the reward, calibration, tracker, and code analysis from noise_aware and the GPU reward and run plumbing from gpu_scale; adds nothing to noise_aware.SETTINGS. The report gives the cross-evaluation matrix per setting and compares the all-to-all codes under the ion profile with the 4x4 lattice cells of experiments/gpu_scale/runs/ (read from their JSON files), the rotated surface code's polished lattice encoder (experiments/noise_aware/runs/baselines_4x4.json) and, from the baselines subcommand, its all-to-all encoder, and the n = 16 codes of known_codes, with seed-level permutation tests. tests/test_ion_chain.py (2 items, skipped without torch).
  • Multi-round memory objective (memory_objective; design note docs/memory_objective.md, runs in experiments/memory_objective/REPORT.md). A code is scored by the logical error rate per round of an R-round syndrome-extraction memory experiment instead of by its encoder's single-fault mass, which cannot see a local-Clifford deformation of the code (experiments/noise_aware/runs/REPORT.md). build_memory_circuit builds the circuit for arbitrary (non-CSS) generators: one ancilla per generator with controlled-X/Y/Z gates, hook-aware gate orders (hook_orders, the ion-search suffix and segment criterion, exact completion cost from the Knill-Laflamme kernel), generators that share a qubit with different letters in separate batches so the interleaved gates commute (X block then Z block for CSS codes), optional one-flag ancillas, noiseless MPP preparation and readout, detectors between consecutive rounds. Layouts: all-to-all (ion chain) and square:RxC with ancilla sites at the plaquette centers and nearest-neighbour CNOT ladders for non-local generators. Tiers: proxy (leading-order failure of the maximum-likelihood decoder over fault sets of weight at most two from the DEM, plus exact d_circ up to weight 4, exact_dcirc ported from ion-search/lib.py), sampled (exact ML decoder by dynamic program when D + O <= 20, else a weight-2 lookup decoder), bposd (the board's pinned BP+OSD, needs ldpc, validation only). MemoryReward is the environment reward (distance and padding terms of the noise-aware experiment plus weight * log10(p_ref / p_round) on target-distance states, cached per code) and exposes success_fn; CodeDiscoveryEnv adopts a reward's success_fn attribute when none is given. experiments.memory_objective (run as python -m): tier benchmark on [[5,1,3]], Steane, rotated surface, the board's [[16,4,4]], and a discovered non-CSS [[9,1,3]] under the chain, board, and Heron profiles; Spearman correlation of the proxy against bposd on 32 random [[9,1,3]] codes; the XZZX bias-sensitivity sweep; the lattice routing comparison; a PPO smoke run on the 3x3 lattice under the ion profile. tests/test_memory_objective.py (14 items, the PPO smoke regression skipped without torch).
  • PPO with the memory objective on the 4x4 setting (experiments.memory_ppo, run as python -m; report in experiments/memory_ppo/REPORT.md, runs in experiments/memory_ppo/runs/): the noise-aware 4x4 protocol of gpu_scale (equivariant policy, batch 1024, H and CNOT on square:4x4, 50-gate episodes, fractional distance term, padding and LDPC penalties) with the memory term of MemoryReward (R = 4 rounds, all-to-all layout, proxy tier, both bases) in place of the encoder's undetected fault mass, on four cells: the chain preset at scale 0.25 with bare and with one-flag ancillas, the board recipe at 0.25, and the Heron rates at 0.05 (the benchmark scales board 1 and Heron 0.1 put the R = 4 circuits above one expected fault per shot, outside the tiers' regime). TorchMemoryReward evaluates the distance, fractional, and padding terms on the device through gpu_scale.DistanceKernel and the memory term on the host in a spawn process pool (MemoryTermPool, one evaluation per distinct stabilizer group, synchronous with the training loop). score evaluates the best code of every run, the nine encoder-objective 4x4 codes of experiments/gpu_scale/runs, and the rotated surface [[16,1,4]] with its XZZX deformation under the four profiles at the proxy and the bposd tier; report writes the tables and figures. Result of the 12-run matrix (RunPod A40, 150 min per run, host CPU capped at four cores): every run reaches d = 4, but under the validation decoder the memory-trained best codes are 8.9 to 50 times worse than the rotated surface code on their training profile and not distinguishable from the encoder-trained codes; no Hadamard frame or d_X/d_Z asymmetry beyond the encoder's own appears under the ion profile; the proxy tier underestimates the discovered codes 5 to 20 times (sampled tier agrees with bposd) because their memory circuits carry 0.9 to 1.5 expected faults per shot. Run 2 (--variant run2, experiments/memory_ppo/runs/run2/, second section of the report): no LDPC term, selection by the training p_round, a gate-count term above 1.25 times the surface code's two-qubit gates per round, the sampled tier for candidates above 0.8 expected faults per shot, and every code evaluated on the sparsest basis of its stabilizer group (sparsest_code; the memory circuit measures the generators it is given, and the encoder tableau's basis is denser than the sparsest one, which inflated every run-1 discovered-code number 3 to 10 times). The run-2 selected codes are 0.8 to 3.1 times the surface code under bposd on their training profile (median 1.8) against 1.8 to 5.3 (median 2.6) for the run-1 codes re-scored the same way; one board seed is at parity. tests/test_memory_ppo.py (5 items, skipped without torch).
  • memory_objective._joint_ids: the multi-word path (more than 64 detectors, every n = 16 memory circuit) labels the pair signatures by a lexsort of the word columns instead of np.unique(axis=0) (whose structured-view argsort took 14 of the 19 s of one proxy evaluation of a dense [[16,1,4]] code), and shifts the labels when the all-zero signature is absent, since the maximum-likelihood grouping tests id == 0 for the zero syndrome (before, the smallest nonzero signature took that role). Test added.

First cut.

  • Batched Aaronson-Gottesman tableau (tableau) with H, S, S_DAG, CNOT, CZ, SWAP, and Pauli frames applied to selected batch elements with per-element qubit indices; stim conversion and random-circuit agreement tests.
  • Symplectic and GF(2) helpers (symplectic): logical operators by symplectic Gram-Schmidt, tableau completion from stabilizers.
  • Pauli error sets by weight and by channel probability (errors).
  • Knill-Laflamme reward of Olle et al., batched exact-distance reward, low-weight-stabilizer penalty, composite rewards (reward).
  • StabilizerCode with exact distance for n <= 20, randomized upper bound with witness for larger n, CSS test, weight enumerators (code); reference codes [[5,1,3]], Steane, Shor, rotated surface [[9,1,3]], [[4,2,2]] (known_codes).
  • Connectivity graphs: all-to-all, linear, square, triangular, heavy-hex (graphs).
  • Gymnasium-style batched environment (env), no gymnasium dependency.
  • Circuit-level noise hook with single-fault propagation through stim and a placeholder depolarizing model (circuit_noise).
  • Random and evolutionary search agents (search); rediscovery regression for [[5,1,3]], Steane, and the rotated surface code with results JSON (regress, autoqec-regress CLI).

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text:
Issues and pull requests are welcome at the repository.

Setup and checks.

git clone https://github.com/unitaryfoundation/autoqec-sim && cd autoqec-sim
uv sync --group dev --extra rl     # plain `uv sync --group dev` skips torch and the PPO tests
uv run ruff check
uv run pytest                      # about 70 s; the reduced regressions are in the suite

Rules of the repository:

  • The reward engine is numpy on CPU by design; keep the state as the one (batch, 2n, 2n+1) uint8 array and the hot path in the kernels listed in docs/gpu.md, so a GPU backend can replace them without touching the surrounding code.
  • A change that affects search results reruns the full-budget regressions and updates experiments/regression/regression.json or experiments/regression/regression_ppo.json and the tables in docs/experiments.md (docs/reproduce.md has the commands).
  • New reward terms or constraints get a verification independent of the reward (exact distance, enumerators), as regress does.
  • Add a CHANGELOG.md entry under the upcoming version.
  • Prose: no em dashes, Oxford comma, terse.

Commits are authored by their author; no generated-with or co-author trailers.

docs.title: Releasing
docs.text: Releases are tagged on main. There is no PyPI package: the release artifacts are the sdist and wheel attached to the GitHub release, the Zenodo DOI, and the versioned documentation.

docs.title: Before the first release
docs.text:
Decisions that only the owner can take, each needed before v0.2.0 is tagged:

  • The institutional copyright holder named in LICENSE (a question for Unitary Foundation agreements and IonQ).
  • The author list of CITATION.cff, which currently has none. GitHub's "Cite this repository" button and Zenodo's author metadata both read it.
  • Whether to publish on PyPI. The current decision is no: the proposal and the data-management plan ask for a public GitHub release with a Zenodo DOI, and the release workflow attaches the sdist and wheel to the GitHub release only.

Zenodo must be enabled for the repository on zenodo.org before the tag is pushed, since its GitHub integration archives only releases created after it is switched on, and the repository must be public for that. Once the release exists, paste the concept DOI into CITATION.cff and commit.

tools/release.sh vX.Y.Z runs the mechanical part: it dates CITATION.cff and CHANGELOG.md, switches the README's documentation links from dev/ to stable/, commits, makes the repository public, tags, and pushes.

docs.title: Prepare
docs.text:
1. Set the version in pyproject.toml and autoqec_sim.__version__; tests/test_version.py pins them together.
  2. Date the version's entry in CHANGELOG.md and set date-released in CITATION.cff.
  3. Update "What's New" on the documentation home page (docs/index.md) with a short summary of the release and links to the new pages.
  4. Build and check the documentation: uv run --group docs mkdocs build. The configuration is strict, so a broken link or an unresolved API reference fails the build.

docs.title: Tag
docs.text:
git tag -a vX.Y.Z -m "autoqec-sim X.Y.Z"
git push origin vX.Y.Z

The release workflow checks that the tag equals uv version --short, builds the sdist and wheel, installs the wheel into a clean environment, attaches both to a GitHub release, and then publishes the documentation for X.Y.Z with the stable alias and makes stable the site's default version.

docs.title: Documentation versions
docs.text:
Documentation is versioned with mike. Pushes to main publish the unreleased documentation to https://unitaryfoundation.github.io/autoqec-sim/dev/. A release tag publishes https://unitaryfoundation.github.io/autoqec-sim/X.Y.Z/ and points stable at it. Until the first release, the site root redirects to dev; afterwards it redirects to stable. The version selector in the header lists every published version.

docs.title: Choose a Workflow
docs.text:
The package separates the search space (qubits, gate set, connectivity), the reward, the agent, and where the kernels run. Start from the result you need.

I want to... Start with Rediscover a known code and check the installation autoqec-regress --budget reduced; Rediscovery regression Train PPO on the same targets autoqec-ppo --budget reduced (rl extra); PPO agent Search for a code under my own n, k, graph, and gate set CodeDiscoveryEnv with EvolutionarySearch or agents.ppo; User Guide Score an encoding circuit under a device noise model circuit_noise.circuit_level_reward with a preset; Noise interface, Device presets Score a code by a multi-round memory experiment with a decoder memory_objective.MemoryReward; Memory objective Require sparse stabilizers ldpc_w_max on the environment or ldpc_penalty in the reward; LDPC constraint Noisify a stim.Circuit of my own autoqec_sim.noise.apply; Noise interface Assign CX layers of a syndrome-extraction circuit for a fixed code autoqec-schedule <slug> --board <path>; Commands Run the reward engine on a GPU backends.torch_backend, backends.cuda_kernels; GPU backend Reproduce the published tables tools/reproduce.sh; Reproduce Read what the discovery agent has and has not found Experiments

docs.title: Which agent
docs.text: The evolutionary search needs only numpy, runs one batched rollout per generation, and is the agent of autoqec-regress. PPO needs torch, uses action masking (the connectivity graph, an undo mask, and any mask the environment exposes), and matched the evolutionary search on every rediscovery target with 3 to 17 times fewer state evaluations in the full-budget regression. For lattices, the permutation-equivariant policy in agents.policies is the one the experiments use.

docs.title: Which reward
docs.text: Reward Module Scores Cost Knill-Laflamme reward.kl_reward undetected mass over an enumerated Pauli error set one GF(2) product per error set Exact distance reward and code.StabilizerCode the minimum weight in the normalizer minus the stabilizer enumeration, n <= 20 LDPC penalty or constraint ldpc minimum bottleneck generator weight w* and qubit degree bit-packed elimination, n - k <= 14 exact Circuit-level noise circuit_noise undetected single-fault mass of the noisy encoder under a profile one fault set per circuit, propagated with one GF(2) product Memory objective memory_objective logical error rate per round of an R-round syndrome-extraction circuit proxy, exact-ML or lookup sampling, or BP+OSD sampling

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
pip install git+https://github.com/unitaryfoundation/autoqec-sim

This installs main. autoqec-sim is not published on PyPI; to install a release, append its tag, for example ...autoqec-sim@v0.2.0.

Python 3.12 to 3.14

The package runs on Python 3.12, 3.13, and 3.14. Its only dependencies are numpy and stim 1.

docs.title: Extras
docs.text:
Extra Adds Needed for rl torch the PPO agent, autoqec-ppo, autoqec-schedule, and the torch backend 
pip install "autoqec-sim[rl] @ git+https://github.com/unitaryfoundation/autoqec-sim"

Without the extra, the evolutionary search, autoqec-regress, and every reward run on numpy.

docs.title: GPU
docs.text:
The torch backend runs on any CUDA device that torch sees. Install a CUDA build of torch for your driver, then install autoqec-sim without the rl extra so the CUDA build is kept. In this repository, uv sync --extra rl pins torch to the CPU-only index on Linux, so on a GPU host use pip install -e . into an environment that already has CUDA torch.

The two fused CUDA kernels in autoqec_sim.backends.cuda_kernels are compiled at first use through CuPy's NVRTC path and need cupy for the installed CUDA version. They are opt-in: set AUTOQEC_CUDA_KERNELS=1 or call cuda_kernels.enable(). GPU backend has the procedure and the measurements.

uv sync --group dev --extra rl     # plain `uv sync --group dev` skips torch and the PPO tests
uv run pytest                      # about 70 s; the reduced regressions are in the suite

docs.title: Score a code
docs.text:
MemoryObjective builds the syndrome-extraction circuit of any stabilizer code, noisifies it under a device profile, and returns the logical error per round from its detector error model. Here the three codes are known ones; a code from any other tool goes in the same way through StabilizerCode.from_stabilizers. The Forte preset runs at a quarter of its measured rates, the scale the experiments use.

from autoqec_sim import known_codes
from autoqec_sim.memory_objective import MemoryObjective
from autoqec_sim.noise import presets

# A three-round memory experiment under the IonQ Forte preset at a quarter of
# its measured rates, scored by the low-weight maximum-likelihood proxy.
objective = MemoryObjective(presets.forte("sequential"), scale=0.25, rounds=3)
for name in ("five_qubit", "steane", "rotated_surface_9"):
    code = known_codes.get(name)
    print(name, code.parameters(), f"error per round {objective.evaluate(code).p_round:.2e}")

five_qubit (5, 1, 3) error per round 4.26e-03
steane (7, 1, 3) error per round 2.09e-03
rotated_surface_9 (9, 1, 3) error per round 5.89e-04

docs.title: Search for a code
docs.text:
A CodeDiscoveryEnv holds batch_size encoding circuits on n qubits encoding k logical qubits. Its default reward is the Knill-Laflamme undetected mass over all Paulis below the target distance of 3, and its default gate set is H, S, and CNOT on all-to-all connectivity. The evolutionary search evolves gate sequences until one reaches the target reward, and StabilizerCode.from_gates reads the code off the winning circuit. This is docs/examples/quickstart.py; it runs in under a second.

from autoqec_sim import CodeDiscoveryEnv, EvolutionarySearch, StabilizerCode

env = CodeDiscoveryEnv(n=5, k=1, batch_size=512, seed=0)
result = EvolutionarySearch(env, seed=0).run(max_evaluations=30_000)

code = StabilizerCode.from_gates(5, 1, result.gates)
print(code.parameters(), code.stabilizer_strings())

(5, 1, 3) ['-ZZIYX', '+IXXZX', '+XIYXX', '-ZXYIY']

A [[5,1,3]] code, the only distance-3 code on five qubits.

docs.title: Verify and score
docs.text: The rest of this page rediscovers the [[5,1,3]] code with the regression's target, verifies it independently of the reward, and scores its encoding circuit under a device noise profile. The whole script is docs/examples/rediscover_and_score.py and runs in about two seconds.

docs.title: Search
docs.text:
A CodeDiscoveryEnv holds batch_size encoding circuits as one array of stabilizer tableaux on n qubits encoding k logical qubits. Each step applies one gate from gates to every batch element. The regression's target for the [[5,1,3]] code fixes the gate set (H, S, CNOT on five all-to-all qubits), the gate cap, and the reward: the Knill-Laflamme term over all weight-1 and weight-2 Paulis plus a penalty on weight-1 stabilizers.

from autoqec_sim.env import CodeDiscoveryEnv
from autoqec_sim.regress import TARGETS, make_reward
from autoqec_sim.search import EvolutionarySearch

# Batched environment: 512 parallel episodes on 5 all-to-all qubits with
# H, S, and CNOT, at most 14 gates; the reward is the Knill-Laflamme term
# over all weight-1 and weight-2 Paulis plus the weight-1 stabilizer penalty.
target = TARGETS["five_qubit"]
env = CodeDiscoveryEnv(n=5, k=1, batch_size=512, gates=target.gates, max_steps=target.max_steps,
                       reward_fn=make_reward(target), seed=0)
res = EvolutionarySearch(env, seed=0).run(max_evaluations=30_000)
print(f"search: success={res.success} evaluations={res.evaluations} gates={len(res.gates)} wall={res.wall_time_s:.1f} s")

docs.title: Verify
docs.text:
Replay the found gate sequence on a fresh tableau and read the code off it. StabilizerCode computes the exact distance and the weight enumerators of the stabilizer group and its normalizer, which are compared with the reference code. This check does not use the reward.

import numpy as np

from autoqec_sim import BatchTableau, StabilizerCode, known_codes

# Replay the found gate sequence on a fresh tableau and read the code off it.
tab = BatchTableau(5, 1)
for gate, a, b in res.gates:
    tab.apply(gate, a, b if b >= 0 else None)
code = StabilizerCode.from_tableau(tab.array, k=1)
ref = known_codes.get("five_qubit")
print(f"code: n={code.n} k={code.k} d={code.distance_exact()} css={code.is_css()}")
match = all(np.array_equal(a, b) for a, b in zip(code.weight_enumerators(), ref.weight_enumerators(), strict=True))
print("enumerators match [[5,1,3]]:", match)

The code has distance 3, is not CSS, and its enumerators match the reference.

docs.title: Score under device noise
docs.text:
circuit_level_reward lays the gate list out as a TICK-layered circuit, applies a noise profile, propagates every single-fault mechanism to the output with stim, and returns minus the undetected mass. The IonQ Forte preset at a quarter of its measured rates is one of the device presets.

from autoqec_sim.circuit_noise import circuit_level_reward
from autoqec_sim.noise import presets

# Circuit-level score: every single-fault mechanism of the encoding circuit
# under the IonQ Forte profile, propagated with stim, as -undetected mass.
r = circuit_level_reward(tab.array, 1, [res.gates], presets.forte(), scale=0.25)
print(f"circuit-level reward under forte @ 0.25: {r[0]:.4f}")

docs.title: Noisify a circuit of your own
docs.text:
The noise module also works on a plain stim.Circuit. A skeleton in the TICK-layer convention is noisified under a preset, and the detector error model gives the mechanism count and the expected number of faults. The script is docs/examples/noise_quickstart.py.

import stim

from autoqec_sim import noise as nm
from autoqec_sim.noise import presets

# Three-qubit repetition code, one round, in the TICK-layer convention:
# data qubits 0, 2, 4 and one ancilla per Z check (qubits 1, 3).
skeleton = stim.Circuit("""
    R 0 1 2 3 4
    TICK
    CX 0 1 2 3
    TICK
    CX 2 1 4 3
    TICK
    M 1 3
    DETECTOR rec[-2]
    DETECTOR rec[-1]
    TICK
    M 0 2 4
    OBSERVABLE_INCLUDE(0) rec[-3]
""")

# IonQ Forte preset at a quarter of its measured rates (p2 = 1e-3).
noisy = nm.apply(skeleton, presets.forte(), scale=0.25)
dem = nm.dem(noisy)
print(noisy)
print("mechanisms:", nm.mechanism_count(dem), "expected faults:", round(nm.fault_expectation(dem), 5))

# Superconducting preset on a line graph, Z-biased tenfold, one two-qubit
# gate per time slot; gates off the graph raise ConnectivityError.
profile = presets.heron(graph=nm.path(5)).with_bias(10.0).with_timing(nm.partial(1))
print(nm.summarize(profile, scale=1.0))
print("exact DEM:", profile.dem_exact, "layers:", str(nm.apply(skeleton, profile, 1.0)).count("TICK") + 1)

docs.title: autoqec-regress
docs.text:
The known-code rediscovery regression with the evolutionary search. --budget reduced is what the test suite runs; --budget full produced experiments/regression/regression.json. Rediscovery regression lists the targets and Reproduce the expected outputs.

usage: autoqec-regress [-h] [--budget {full,reduced}] [--seed SEED]
                       [--targets [TARGET ...]] [--out OUT] [--verbose]

options:
  --budget {full,reduced}
  --seed SEED
  --targets [TARGET ...]  five_qubit, steane, rotated_surface_9,
                          rotated_surface_9_ldpc, rotated_surface_9_ldpc_penalty,
                          steane_ldpc_w4, seven_qubit_w3_excluded,
                          five_qubit_w3_excluded
  --out OUT               results JSON path
  --verbose

docs.title: autoqec-ppo
docs.text:
The same regression with PPO in place of the evolutionary search, plus the PPO-only 4x4 rotated-surface target rotated_surface_16 at the full budget. --compare takes the evolutionary results JSON for a side-by-side table.

usage: autoqec-ppo [-h] [--budget {full,reduced}] [--seed SEED]
                   [--targets [TARGET ...]] [--out OUT] [--compare COMPARE]
                   [--threads THREADS] [--verbose]

options:
  --budget {full,reduced}
  --seed SEED
  --targets [TARGET ...]  the autoqec-regress targets and rotated_surface_16
  --out OUT               results JSON path
  --compare COMPARE       evolutionary results JSON
  --threads THREADS       torch and BLAS thread cap (default 6)
  --verbose

docs.title: autoqec-schedule
docs.text:
CX-layer schedule synthesis for the syndrome-extraction circuit of a fixed code from a qldpc-challenge board. The command scores the board builder's own schedules as baselines, trains a PPO policy on the exact circuit fault distance, and confirms the best schedule at rounds = d with the board's search tier. On the [[49,13,4]] circuit it raised the fault distance from 2 to 3.

usage: autoqec-schedule [-h] [--updates UPDATES] [--batch BATCH]
                        [--baseline BASELINE] [--tier {exact,ris}]
                        [--ris-trials RIS_TRIALS] [--rounds ROUNDS]
                        [--interleave] [--slack SLACK]
                        [--depth-penalty DEPTH_PENALTY]
                        [--edge-order {fixed,shuffle}] [--seed SEED]
                        [--confirm-trials CONFIRM_TRIALS] [--out OUT]
                        [--board BOARD]
                        slug

positional arguments:
  slug                  board code slug, for example 49-13-4

options:
  --rounds ROUNDS       extraction rounds scored (default: screen at 2,
                        confirm at d)
  --tier {exact,ris}    fault-distance tier
  --out OUT             output directory (default schedule_out/<slug>)
  --board BOARD         qldpc-challenge checkout (default: QLDPC_CHALLENGE or
                        a sibling directory)

autoqec_sim.schedule_env and autoqec_sim.schedule_cli are documented in the Python API.
